target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102011: When the OpenClaw tool schema injects `flowExpectedRevision=0` as a default value, the Lobster plugin's `parseRunFlowParams` and `parseResumeFlowParams` treated this as an intentional TaskFlow signal, causing ordinary `run` and `resume` calls to fail with:
- `run action does not accept flowId or flowExpectedRevision`
- `flowExpectedRevision required when using managed TaskFlow resume mode`

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a positive `flowExpectedRevision` (> 0) signals intentional TaskFlow mode. Schema default `0` means the caller did not supply this field — it should be treated as absent. The fix applies to both `parseRunFlowParams` and `parseResumeFlowParams`:

- **run**: Only reject when `flowExpectedRevision > 0`
- **resume**: Only enter TaskFlow mode when `flowExpectedRevision > 0`; the validation error is also updated to require a positive value

## Evidence

- [x] `pnpm test extensions/lobster/src/lobster-tool.test.ts` — 19 tests pass (incl. 2 new)

target.title: fix(telegram): silently skip empty-text sends
target.body:
Supersedes #59725 (auto-closed by the 10-open-PR cap; not reopenable because the close `stateReason` is `COMPLETED` and the branch was force-pushed since). ## Scope note: re-derived on top of current main Most of the original branch scope has since landed on `main` through other work, so this PR was reset onto `main` and re-implemented to cover only the residual gaps: - #56620 added `filterEmptyTelegramTextChunks` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.replies.ts`), which already drops whitespace-only chunks before any send. - The `sendTelegramText` rewrite around `sendPlainFallback` / `buildTelegramPlainFallbackPlan` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts`) already recovers formatted-send failures when a non-empty plain fallback exists. - #93279 introduced the default-vs-rich delivery split, which this PR preserves: the rich lane stays opt-in behind `richMessages === true` and both lanes get the same skip semantics. Two gaps remain on current `main`, and they are exactly the reported user path: 1. `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` only matches Telegram's legacy `message text is empty` wording. The live Bot API now also returns `text must be non-empty` (raw round-trip below), so the empty-text 400 escapes the recovery branch. 2. When non-whitespace source renders to empty visible text and the plain fallback is also empty (for example `` with `plainText: ""`), `main` throws (`empty rich text and empty plain fallback` / `empty formatted text and empty plain fallback`) or rethrows the 400 from the catch block, surfacing a user-visible delivery failure for content the model never made visible. ## Behavior addressed Interrupted mid-reply turns can produce formatted Telegram HTML that has no visible text and no plain-text fallback, for example an empty supported tag such as ``. Telegram rejects that payload with HTTP 400 (`message text is empty` legacy wording, `text must be non-empty` newer wording). Previously this surfaced as a user-visible delivery failure; this PR silently treats that empty-text send as a no-op with correct accounting. Parse errors remain out of scope and still throw (bare `
` payloads fail as parse errors, per the live baseline below). ## Change - `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` now also matches `text must be non-empty` and the rich-lane `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` rejection. - `sendTelegramText` returns `Promise`: when the rendered payload is empty and the plain fallback is also empty, it resolves `undefined` (silent no-op) instead of throwing, both pre-flight and when Telegram rejects the payload as empty. Sends with a usable plain fallback still recover exactly as on `main`; parse errors and unrelated failures still throw. - `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` treats an `undefined` chunk result as a no-op: no `markReplyApplied`, no `markDelivered`, so skipped chunks do not advance reply state, delivered count, transcript mirroring, `message_sent.success`, or pinning, and do not consume the reply target. - Voice fallback text paths mirror only text that actually reached Telegram: an all-skipped caption fallback no longer registers `reply.text` as delivered transcript content. ## Verification Run after this patch (rebased branch head), from a worktree of current `main` + this commit: ``` node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts -> 3 files, 81 tests passed node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram -> 132/133 files passed, 2461/2462 tests passed. The single failure (bot.test.ts "does not retry plugin-owned callback text skipped by inbound policy") fails identically on a clean upstream/main checkout (827f2c4422) and is unrelated to this change. node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json -> clean node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json -> clean node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs -> clean oxfmt --check -> clean ``` ## Live Telegram round-trip Raw Telegram Bot API baseline (no OpenClaw code; still-valid proof of current Telegram wordings, motivating the regex widening): ``` payload="
" expected=parse-error -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unsupported start tag \"br\" at byte offset 0" payload=" " expected=accepted-by-telegram -> OK message_id=10657 payload="" expected=empty-text -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: text must be non-empty" ``` A `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText` was run against the live Bot API for the earlier revision of this branch (head `0a0035aa2818`, before the rebase onto current `main`); it observed `resolved=undefined` for `` with `plainText: ""`, thrown parse errors for bare `
` variants, and a real `message_id` for well-formed payloads. The rebased implementation pins the same `sendTelegramText` contract with the unit tests in `delivery.send.test.ts`; the live driver was not re-run against the rebased head. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Empty visible-text Telegram HTML sends with an empty plain fallback no longer surface as delivery failures; they are treated as no-op sends with no phantom delivery accounting, while parse errors and fallback-capable sends behave as on main. Real environment tested: Live Telegram Bot API (raw `sendMessage` baseline confirming the current `text must be non-empty` wording for ``; grammY driver run against the earlier revision of this branch), plus local Vitest runs of the rebased code against mocked Bot API surfaces. Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts` and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram` on the rebased head. Evidence after fix: 81/81 tests pass across the three delivery test files, including new regressions: `` + `text must be non-empty` resolves `undefined` (one API call, no throw); legacy `message text is empty` wording ditto; render-empty + empty-fallback skips before any API call on both default and rich lanes; empty-text 400 with a non-empty fallback still recovers via plain send; parse errors and unrelated errors still throw; all-skipped replies report `message_sent` `success=false` with no `messageId`, no transcript mirror, no pin, and `delivered: false`. Observed result after fix: Empty-text sends skip silently without advancing reply delivery state; payloads with real content or a usable plain fallback deliver unchanged; bare `
` HTML still throws the Telegram parse error and remains out of scope. What was not tested: The live grammY driver was not re-run against the rebased head (its output above is from the earlier branch revision); no full live interrupted-agent session was exercised. Focused regression tests cover send skipping, reply accounting, transcript mirroring, hooks, pin behavior, and voice fallback paths.

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard container flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup previously required users to hand-configure native `signal-cli` even when they wanted OpenClaw to guide them through a local Signal REST container or an existing Signal API server. It also had setup/status gaps where transport mode, receive readiness, and multi-account setup state could be misreported or persisted on the wrong account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now owns native, Docker container, and existing-server setup paths inside the Signal plugin, while core setup gains only the generic `setupApplied` rollback signal needed to avoid persisting failed or cancelled setup attempts. Managed Docker setup verifies the account-specific `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket before saving container setup, and the branch is rebased onto current `main` while preserving current-main Signal container attachment hardening.

## User Impact

Users can configure Signal through the setup wizard with a Docker container flow, QR/linking guidance, and existing-server reconfiguration that does not require re-entering an already saved Signal number. Operators get clearer `channels status` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states, and mixed multi-account configs keep transport fields scoped to the intended account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Docker setup verifies `/v1/receive/{account}` before every managed setup success return: single listed account, selected account from multiple linked accounts, and newly linked QR account.
- Non-interactive existing-server setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "auto"` and `autoStart: false`, so a previous container setup does not force a later `--http-url` config through the container adapter.
- Non-interactive native setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: true`, and clears `httpUrl`, so a later `--cli-path`/host/port setup does not keep using an old external server.
- Failed or cancelled setup returns `setupApplied: false`, so core setup skips account selection hooks, setup callbacks, completion notes, and partial config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts.
- Signal status/probe output exposes readiness-specific states instead of collapsing account-missing or receive-unavailable probes into generic working/unreachable output.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard and gateway status behavior; the reviewer-checkable proof is command/test output and config transition coverage.

Automated checks run on rebased head `99b74ffa5db50b442f271c522516fb05865f1b52`:

target.title: fix: gate Gateway message action requester provenance [AI]

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a write-scoped Gateway client could provide requester identity fields on `message.action` requests and have that identity treated as trusted channel provenance by downstream message actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now treats requester account and sender provenance like other trusted channel-action context: only full-scope callers can bridge server-injected requester identity through the public RPC boundary. Write-scoped clients can still invoke supported message actions, but their caller-supplied requester identity and owner bit are stripped before channel dispatch.

## User Impact

Operators keep the existing `message.action` workflow for normal write-scoped clients, while channel actions that depend on trusted sender identity no longer accept spoofed requester provenance from those clients. This narrows the authorization boundary without changing channel configuration, storage, migrations, or plugin manifests.

target.title: feat: add WhatsApp phone-code login
target.body:
Closes #85867

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users trying to connect WhatsApp from a headless, remote, or QR-unavailable environment had no first-class login path. OpenClaw only exposed the WhatsApp QR flow, so users who could not scan a QR code could not link WhatsApp even though WhatsApp Linked Devices supports phone-number pairing.

It also fixes a session-state edge case where partial phone-code pairing credentials could look linked enough to block a clean retry, even though the WhatsApp account was not fully registered.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed channel login method for phone-number login, exposes it through `openclaw channels login whatsapp --phone-number <number>`, and keeps QR login as the default path. The generic CLI/channel contract carries a structured `phone-number` login method, while the WhatsApp plugin owns the Baileys `requestPairingCode` implementation, pairing-code display, retry behavior, and cleanup of stale partial pairing credentials.

The change intentionally keeps WhatsApp-specific policy inside the WhatsApp plugin and only adds the small shared channel-auth contract needed for channels to advertise and receive non-QR login methods.

## User Impact

Users can now link WhatsApp by entering their phone number in the CLI and then entering the generated code in WhatsApp's Linked Devices flow. QR login still works for users who prefer it or have a scannable terminal session.

If a phone-code attempt leaves behind incomplete credentials, the next login can clear that stale partial state and let the user retry instead of treating the account as already connected.

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback now rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait:

- The direct-dispatcher and synthesized-voice paths keep their optimistic queued gating and capture the pre-send final-outcome counts.
- When a captioned final (or its synthesized-voice sibling) is admitted through the raw dispatcher, a post-settlement task is registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` — the same seam the transcript mirror uses. It runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path.
- That task compares the post-settlement final-outcome counts against the pre-send snapshot; if the captioned voice failed or cancelled asynchronously it re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final, so suppressed content is never silently dropped. On success it does nothing, so there is no duplicate text.

This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix(lobster): don't route schema-default flowExpectedRevision into TaskFlow (#102011)
target.body:
Closes #102011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ordinary `@openclaw/lobster` tool `run` / `resume` calls
fail by being misrouted into managed TaskFlow mode. When the tool schema supplies
default flow fields for a minimal call — `flowExpectedRevision` (e.g. `0`) or an
empty `flowStateJson` — the wrapper treated those always-present values as a
managed-flow signal, so an ordinary `resume` errored with `flowId required when
using managed TaskFlow resume mode` and an ordinary `run` with `flowControllerId
required when using managed TaskFlow run mode` / `run action does not accept
flowId or flowExpectedRevision`. The standalone Lobster CLI handled the same
workflow correctly, confirming the fault is in the OpenClaw plugin wrapper.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed TaskFlow mode is identified only by its intentional flow identifiers —
`flowId` for `resume`, `flowControllerId`/`flowGoal` for `run`. Secondary fields
(`flowExpectedRevision`, `flowStateJson`, and the step fields), which the tool
schema can inject as defaults, no longer select managed mode on their own. Real
managed flows are unchanged: managed `resume` still requires
`flowExpectedRevision`, and managed `run` still needs `flowControllerId`/`flowGoal`.

## User Impact

The documented minimal `run` / `resume` Lobster tool calls work again; ordinary
approval workflows no longer fail with a spurious managed-TaskFlow error.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — drove the actual `createLobsterTool` with the **real
embedded `@clawdbot/lobster` runtime** executing the issue's `approval-smoke`
workflow, passing the schema-injected defaults (`flowExpectedRevision: 0`,
`flowStateJson: "{}"`) on the minimal `run`, then `resume` with the returned
token:

```
BEFORE (current source): the ordinary run is misrouted into managed mode and the
  real lobster runtime call fails with:
    Error: flowControllerId required when using managed TaskFlow run mode
AFTER (this PR): run → needs_approval (real resumeToken), then resume → ok.
  The full run→approval→resume completes through the real runtime.
```

(Ran via a temporary `*.test.ts` using `createEmbeddedLobsterRunner()`; captured
the before/after by toggling the source with `git stash`. Not committed.)

**Regression tests** in `extensions/lobster/src/lobster-tool.test.ts` (colocated,
run the real `createLobsterTool`):
- ordinary `resume` carrying only a schema-default `flowExpectedRevision` runs as
  an ordinary resume instead of erroring;
- ordinary `run` carrying only a schema-default `flowStateJson` runs as an
  ordinary run instead of erroring;
- managed `run` with an injected `flowExpectedRevision: 0` is still accepted.

Full suite passes (20 tests) via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run
extensions/lobster/src/lobster-tool.test.ts`. oxfmt/oxlint clean.

---

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. The before/after evidence is from running
the real lobster runtime locally, not AI-generated assertions taken on faith.

target.title: fix(gateway): fail fast on missing local probe auth
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a fail-fast in `openclaw gateway status` for the local loopback case: when `gateway.auth.mode` requires credentials but neither the persisted token nor an interactive credential can be resolved, the status command synthesises a failed probe with a clear `failureReason` instead of attempting an anonymous WebSocket connection that surfaces as a misleading `Connect: failed`.

Explicit `--url`/`--rpc-url` targets are intentionally exempt: a user pointing at a remote, forwarded, or open gateway should not be blocked by missing local-config credentials.

## Details

- `resolveAuthForTarget` resolves through the probe-surface helper. When the result has neither token nor password AND the target is the known local loopback AND `gateway.auth.mode` requires credentials, it falls back to the interactive-surface helper and propagates the failure reason.
- The fail-fast is scoped to `surface === "local" && target.kind === "localLoopback"`. Targets with `kind === "explicit"` (i.e. `--url`/`--rpc-url`) skip the check.
- Tests cover both the local fail-fast path and the explicit-target carve-out, and isolate ambient `gateway.auth.token` env in the probe-auth test to avoid cross-test contamination.
- Review follow-ups (head `a4b92bef28`): when the missing-local-auth fail-fast synthesizes the daemon status rpc failure, the restart-health pass is skipped too, so `inspectGatewayRestart` no longer runs the unauthenticated loopback re-probe the fail-fast avoided. The unresolved-SecretRef warning is split so fail-fast results no longer claim "probing without configured auth credentials" when no probe ran.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: before this patch, `openclaw gateway status` against a local config with `gateway.auth.mode: "token"` but an unresolvable token (e.g. `secrets.token.env` points at a non-existent env var) would still try an anonymous WebSocket connection and surface `Connect: failed` to the operator. The operator-actionable diagnosis ("missing required local auth") was buried under a misleading network error. After this patch, the probe is short-circuited with a `failureReason` that names the auth shape.

- **Real environment tested**: two real runs. (1) Gateway status: `openclaw` runtime built from an earlier PR head on a local laptop checkout, run against an isolated test config at `/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json` so the live gateway and its real auth are not touched. (2) Daemon status: current PR head `a4b92bef28` (rebased onto current `upstream/main` `22376d80e1`) run from the source checkout via the repo CLI entry (`tsx src/entry.ts daemon status`) on macOS, with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at a scratch state dir whose config sets `gateway.auth.mode: "token"` and `gateway.auth.token` as an env SecretRef (`MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, unset in the shell); no live gateway/service was touched.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  unset OPENCLAW_PROBE_NONEXISTENT_TEST_VAR
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json node dist/index.js gateway status --json | jq '.rpc | {ok, error, kind}'
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json node dist/index.js gateway status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --json | jq '{rpc: .rpc | {ok, error, kind}, probeUrl: .gateway.probeUrl}'
  # daemon status path, at head a4b92bef28 (paths redacted to <scratch>):
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/state/openclaw.json node_modules/.bin/tsx src/entry.ts daemon status
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/state/openclaw.json node_modules/.bin/tsx src/entry.ts daemon status --json --timeout 3000
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: Captured live from the patched runtime. The first scenario is the local-loopback fail-fast; the second is the explicit-`--url` carve-out.

  ```
  $ node dist/index.js gateway status --json | jq '.rpc | {ok, error, kind}'
  {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "Missing gateway auth token.",
    "kind": null
  }

  $ node dist/index.js gateway status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --json | jq '{rpc: .rpc | {ok, error, kind}, probeUrl: .gateway.probeUrl}'
  {
    "rpc": {
      "ok": false,
      "error": "connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:18999",
      "kind": "connect"
    },
    "probeUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:18999"
  }
  ```

  Daemon status path, captured at head `a4b92bef28` (redacted: scratch state paths shortened to `<scratch>`):

  ```
  $ openclaw daemon status
  Service: LaunchAgent (not loaded)
  Config (cli): <scratch>/state/openclaw.json
  Config (service): <scratch>/state/openclaw.json

  Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=18789 (env/config)
  Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789

  Runtime: unknown (Bad request.
  Could not find service "ai.openclaw.gateway" in domain for user gui: 501)
  Connectivity probe: failed
  Probe auth: gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved in this command path.
  Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
    gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN).

  Service unit not found.
  Service not installed. Run: openclaw gateway install

  $ openclaw daemon status --json  # rpc excerpt
  "rpc": {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN).",
    "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:18789",
    "authWarning": "gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved in this command path."
  }
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: in the local-loopback scenario, `rpc.kind` is `null` (no probe attempt was made) and `rpc.error` names the actionable auth diagnostic instead of a network error. In the explicit-URL scenario, `rpc.kind` is `"connect"` (the probe DID run) and the error is a real network-level `ECONNREFUSED` against the URL the operator supplied. In the daemon status scenario, `rpc.ok` is `false` with the synthesized SecretRef failure reason, `rpc.authWarning` no longer claims a probe ran ("SecretRef is unresolved in this command path" with no "probing without configured auth credentials" suffix), the gateway version stays `null` (no WebSocket probe was attempted), and no restart-health loopback re-probe runs after the synthetic failure (`status.health` is absent; covered by the `inspectGatewayRestart` not-called assertion in `status.gather.test.ts`).

- **What was not tested**: the explicit-URL daemon `--rpc-url` flag was exercised only via the unit test added in `a4b92bef28` (probe runs against the override despite unresolved local auth), not end-to-end against a live gateway. The restart-health pass against a live loaded service with a genuine (non-synthetic) probe failure was not exercised live; that path is unchanged and covered by existing unit tests. The compatibility question of shipping fail-closed behavior for configured-but-unresolved local credentials (ClawSweeper P1) is a gateway/auth owner decision and is intentionally not resolved by this contributor change.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): support edit and unsend actions
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- WhatsApp message actions could not edit or revoke bot-owned messages.
- The old PR also routed edit/unsend through PN-only JID conversion, which could misroute LID-addressed chats.

Why does this matter now?

- WhatsApp outbound sends already use LID-aware routing. Message mutations need the same routing contract or they can target the wrong chat.

What is the intended outcome?

- Add WhatsApp `edit`, `delete`, and `unsend` actions for bot-owned messages.
- Keep `upload-file` support from current `main` while adding the new gateway actions.
- Use `resolveOutboundJid` for edit/unsend so message keys use the resolved LID JID when available.
- Validate edit text before forwarding the gateway action.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Editing or deleting other users' WhatsApp messages.
- Live WhatsApp server compatibility guarantees beyond Baileys payload construction.

What does success look like?

- `edit` sends a Baileys `{ edit }` payload with `fromMe: true`.
- `delete` and `unsend` send a Baileys `{ delete }` payload with `fromMe: true`.
- PN-to-LID mappings are honored for normal sends, reactions, edit, unsend, and typing presence.

What should reviewers focus on?

- LID-aware routing in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.ts`.
- Gateway action dispatch in `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.ts`.
- `actions.sendMessage` gating and target authorization in `extensions/whatsapp/src/action-runtime.ts`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #14344

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #67378

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

- This refresh addresses the existing PR review blocker about reusing LID-aware routing for edit and unsend.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: WhatsApp edit/unsend now use the same LID-aware outbound JID resolution as normal sends and reactions.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on Linux with Node/pnpm and the real WhatsApp send API seam; temp Baileys auth dir containing `lid-mapping-15555550000.json`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/action-runtime.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-actions.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/send.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/active-listener.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

- Evidence after fix:

```text
✓ createWebSendApi LID resolution (issue #67378) > resolves PN to LID for editMessage
✓ createWebSendApi LID resolution (issue #67378) > resolves PN to LID for unsendMessage
Test Files  7 passed (7)
Tests  144 passed (144)
```

- Observed result after fix: edit and unsend calls send to `987654@lid`; their message keys use `remoteJid: "987654@lid"`, `id: "msg-2"`, and `fromMe: true`.
- What was not tested: live WhatsApp account behavior against WhatsApp servers.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: no linked live WhatsApp account was available in this local repair environment, so the proof covers OpenClaw routing, dispatch, gating, payload construction, log sanitization, and listener contracts, not server acceptance.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): the old edit/unsend implementation called `toWhatsappJid(to)`, so a PN target with a LID mapping stayed on `15555550000@s.whatsapp.net` instead of `987654@lid`.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

target.title: fix(telegram): long-running sends leak connections after cache evictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Telegram senders could keep abandoned HTTP transports alive when the Telegram client options cache evicted old account/network entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cache entry now retains the transport created for its client fetch so eviction can release the old dispatcher lifecycle instead of only deleting the client options object. Evicted entries are retired immediately, but their transport is closed only after active Telegram request or operation leases finish, including retry waits and pre-first-request media preparation, so cache pressure does not abort an in-flight, retrying, or still-preparing Telegram send.

## User Impact

Operators running Telegram channels with many account or network option combinations should see stale Telegram transports released after cache eviction instead of accumulating idle connections over time, without changing existing Telegram send behavior for active requests.

## Evidence

- Live/near-real proof passed with a local Telegram Bot API substitute and the real `sendMessageTelegram` entry point. The run sent through 65 distinct production-mode account cache entries, observed 65 HTTP `POST /bot.../sendMessage` requests, and observed 6 undici dispatcher `destroy()` calls after cache eviction.
- Focused Telegram proxy regression passed: 1 file passed, 11 tests passed. The regressions drive 65 production-mode cache entries, verify the evicted transport `close()` is called, verify eviction defers `close()` until the active send finishes, verify eviction waits while a retryable send is sleeping between attempts, verify eviction also waits while media is loading before the first Telegram API request, verify eviction waits while a reaction helper persists a resolved target before its first action request, and verify injected Telegram API callers do not allocate an unused cached transport.
- Extensions type checking passed with `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions`.
- `OPENCLAW_DEV_AUTO_PAIR=false start_openclaw_dev_gateway.sh` — isolated OpenClaw dev gateway reached ready; the startup log recorded `http server listening` and `ready`.

Before the fix, the eviction regression failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` for the evicted transport close spy. Before the retry-window, media-load, and sibling-helper lease fixes, the focused regressions failed because the evicted transport closed while a retryable send was waiting between attempts, while a media send was still loading before its first Telegram API request, and while a reaction helper was still persisting a resolved target before its first action request. The lease regressions cover the active-operation cases that would be unsafe if eviction closed the transport immediately.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
131/131 tests pass across 3 test files (19 + 87 + 25).

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

## Revision (2026-07-07) #1

Removed duplicate heartbeat plugin preactivation path identified by ClawSweeper review:

- **P2 — duplicate startup preactivation**: Removed `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` from `activateGatewayScheduledServices`. The `startHeartbeatRunner` constructor already calls `updateConfig(state.cfg)` which handles the initial preactivation plus all hot-reload/config-update paths. Removing the gateway-side call eliminates a repeated registry scan when an external target fails to load.
- Updated comment in `heartbeat-runner.ts` `updateConfig` to reflect it is now the single preactivation path.
- 147 related tests pass (`server-runtime-services.test.ts`, `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, `targets.test.ts`).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #2 (a0ba292)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — gating preactivation to enabled, deliverable heartbeat configs:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` was called from `updateConfig` before the interval filter (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs`). A disabled heartbeat config (`every: "0m"`) with an external target still triggered `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` during startup/reload, scanning all installed plugins unnecessarily. External targets without a recipient (`to`) were also preactivated even though the runner can never deliver to them.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Config-scan path (startup/reload): each target is only preactivated when the heartbeat is enabled (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` returns non-null) AND has a deliverable recipient (`to` is set). This mirrors the `updateConfig` scheduling loop which skips agents with `intervalMs === 0`.
- Direct heartbeat override path (cron/manual wakes via `requestHeartbeat`): still preactivates without an interval check because the caller already validated the wake is active. Only skips targets without a recipient.

**New regression tests** (+7 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ Disabled default (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Disabled per-agent (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on default target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on per-agent target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on heartbeat override → no preactivation
- ✅ Per-agent with its own `every: "15m"` overrides disabled default → preactivated

**Test results**: 19/19 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass.

## Revision (2026-07-07) #3 (1334dd29)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — skip default target preactivation when explicit per-agent heartbeats override scheduling:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` unconditionally added `agents.defaults.heartbeat` to the target set even when `agents.list[]` entries had their own heartbeat configs. In that case `resolveHeartbeatAgents` schedules only the merged per-agent entries — it does not schedule the default as a standalone target. Preactivating the unused default target caused an unnecessary full-plugin-registry scan on startup/reload.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Added a `hasExplicitAgents` check mirroring `resolveHeartbeatAgents`: when any `agents.list[]` entry has a `heartbeat` block, the standalone default target is skipped. Only the per-agent effective targets (which may merge `target` or `to` from defaults) are preactivated.
- When no agent has an explicit heartbeat, the default target is still preactivated as before (it is what the scheduler runs).

**Updated tests** (+1 new regression, 2 existing tests adjusted):
- ✅ New: "skips the default external target when a per-agent heartbeat overrides it" — default `unused-external-plugin` with `to: room:default` is not preactivated because agent `override-agent` has its own `background-channel` target
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates distinct external targets from defaults and per-agent configs" → now expects only the per-agent target (default skipped)
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates a per-agent external target that inherits to from defaults" → now expects only the per-agent target with inherited `to` (default skipped)

**Test results**: 21/21 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (133 total).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #4 — fix external-target detector (9db74edf)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` used wrong helper semantics:

**Problem**: `isExternalPluginTarget` used `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` and inverted its return value to decide "external plugin." But `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves unknown plugin ids as deliverable (for external-plugin routing), so an explicit external target like `external-channel` made the helper return a truthy value and `isExternalPluginTarget` returned `false` — silently skipping bootstrap preactivation for external plugin targets.

**Root cause in the contract**:
- `normalizeMessageChannel` (in `message-channel-core.ts:27`) preserves unknown-but-normalized ids: `return normalizeAnyChannelId(normalized) ?? normalized`
- `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` wraps `normalizeMessageChannel` + `isDeliverableMessageChannel`, so it returns a truthy value for unknown external plugin channels
- The old `isExternalPluginTarget` inverted this: `return !normalized` — wrong, because the helper returned a value for external channels

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId`
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel(rawTarget)` confirms the target is a deliverable channel id (non-internal, non-empty)
- `!normalizeChatChannelId(rawTarget)` confirms it's NOT a built-in chat channel — built-in channels are already in the bundled catalog and don't need bootstrap
- Only targets that pass both checks (deliverable but not built-in) are classified as external plugin targets

**Updated tests** — `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` mock with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId` mocks
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel` now returns `true` for any non-empty string (matching real contract: unknown plugin ids are deliverable)
- `normalizeChatChannelId` only returns non-null for built-in channel ids (`telegram`, `discord`, `whatsapp`)
- This means external plugin targets (e.g. `external-channel`) correctly pass `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable but not built-in → needs preactivation
- Built-in channel targets (e.g. `telegram`) correctly fail `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable AND built-in → skip preactivation

**Test results**: 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (136 total).



## Revision (2026-07-08)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — explicit normalized heartbeat plugin targets not honoring caller `allowBootstrap`:

**Problem**: When `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves an external plugin channel id (production normalization contract at `message-channel-core.ts:27-29`), the explicit target reaches the later plugin lookup at `targets.ts:217-225`. That lookup hardcoded `allowBootstrap: isSessionDerived` (always `false` for explicit targets) and `allowBundledFallback: !isSessionDerived` (always `true` for explicit targets). This meant:
- Doctor's `allowBootstrap: true` was ignored → false "replies are dropped silently" warnings for external plugin heartbeat targets
- Bundled fallback was enabled on the heartbeat hot path → could lazy-load bundled channel module code contrary to the performance boundary

**Fix in `targets.ts`**:
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget`: plugin lookup now honors `params.allowBootstrap` for explicit targets (`isSessionDerived || params.allowBootstrap === true`) and disables bundled fallback unconditionally (`allowBundledFallback: false`)
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTargetWithSessionRoute`: bundled fallback also disabled in sync with the primary resolution path

**New regression tests** (+2 in `targets.test.ts`):
- ✅ Doctor `allowBootstrap: true` passes through for explicit external targets preserved by production normalization
- ✅ Hot path keeps `allowBootstrap: false` with bundled fallback disabled
- Both tests override the normalization mock to simulate production behavior where external plugin ids are preserved (rather than returning `undefined`)

**Test results**: 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (145 total).


## Revision (2026-07-08) #2 — fix CI lint (9a37f344)

Fixed `check-lint` CI failure (2 `eslint/curly` violations in `targets.test.ts`):

**Problem**: Two newly added test helpers in revision #1 used single-line `if (cond) return val;` without braces — a style rule enforced by `eslint/curly` in CI.

**Fix in `targets.test.ts`**: Added braces to both `if` statements (lines 987, 1026):
```ts
if (normalized === "ext-plugin") {
  return normalized;
}
```

**Test results**: 145/145 pass across 4 test files. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.


## Revision (2026-07-08) — external plugin proof

Real gateway proof with a minimal external channel plugin (`proof-channel`, `deliveryMode: "gateway"`, registered via `openclaw.plugin.json` `channels: ["proof-channel"]`). The plugin is NOT bundled — it lives under `~/.openclaw/extensions/proof-channel/` and is discovered at runtime.

### Setup

- Added `proof-channel` channel plugin to `~/.openclaw/extensions/proof-channel/` (CJS, `deliveryMode: "gateway"`, no bundled fallback)
- Configured `test_agent` with `heartbeat: { target: "proof-channel", to: "proof-test-recipient", every: "30s" }`
- Enabled `proof-channel` in `plugins.entries`
- Added temporary `appendFileSync` probes to capture the preactivation→delivery sequence (reverted before push)

### Gateway startup log

```
[gateway] loading configuration…
[gateway] resolving authentication…
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] starting HTTP server...
[health-monitor] started (interval: 300s, startup-grace: 60s, channel-connect-grace: 120s)
[plugins] proof-channel: loaded without install/load-path provenance; treat as untracked local code.
[heartbeat] started
```

### Proof event timeline

| Phase | Timestamp (UTC) | Event |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| Startup | `02:23:10.748Z` | `preactivate-start` — `hasOverride: false` (config-scan path) |
| Startup | `02:23:10.750Z` | `preactivate-config` — target=`proof-channel`, `targetCount=1`, calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` |
| Tick #1 | `02:23:22.678Z` | `heartbeat-delivery` — target=`proof-channel`, `allowBootstrap: false`, `pluginResolved: true`, `hadPreparedPlugin: false` |
| Tick #2 | `02:24:13.197Z` | `heartbeat-delivery` — target=`proof-channel`, `allowBootstrap: false`, `pluginResolved: true`, `hadPreparedPlugin: false` |

### Key observations

1. **Preactivation done once** — `preactivate-start` fires once at startup (config-scan path). The external plugin target `proof-channel` is resolved with `allowBootstrap: true`, loading it into the active registry.

2. **Hot path stays bootstrap-free** — Both heartbeat ticks deliver with `allowBootstrap: false`. The plugin is already active (`pluginResolved: true`) because preactivation loaded it.

3. **ZERO bootstrap-heavy events** — `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` was never called on the hot path. The `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry` full-plugin-scan was never triggered during wake ticks. If the old `allowBootstrap: true` behavior were still in place, each tick would have triggered a full registry scan for this external plugin channel.

4. **No bundled fallback** — `hadPreparedPlugin: false` confirms delivery follows the explicit-target path, which disables `allowBundledFallback` — the bundled channel module code is never lazy-loaded from the heartbeat hot path.

### Environment

- OS: Linux (x86_64), Node 24.13.1
- Branch: `fix/heartbeat-delivery-bootstrap-latency`
- Commit: `9a37f344d49a7da5e182e750238885538aff5eed` (latest PR head)
- Config: production profile (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) + proof plugin + heartbeat override
- Gateway port: 18790

### What was not tested

- Multi-agent heartbeat with mixed bundled/external targets
- Heartbeat delivery during plugin reload (`updateConfig` hot-reload path)
- Requested heartbeat override wake path (cron/manual wakes with external targets)
- Production external plugins (qqbot, feishu) — proof used a minimal no-network plugin to isolate the registry/preactivation behavior



## Revision (2026-07-08) — normalize target before preactivation classification (d5b03d3)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` checked raw heartbeat target with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` without prior normalization:

**Problem**: Config validation accepts heartbeat targets case-insensitively by lowercasing installed plugin channel ids before membership checks (`src/config/validation.ts:1765`). A config `target: "Proof-Channel"` passes validation and delivery later normalizes it to `proof-channel`, but `isDeliverableMessageChannel("Proof-Channel")` returns `false` (it requires already-normalized input per `message-channel-core.ts:36`). The un-normalized mixed-case target was silently skipped, leaving the external plugin un-preloaded — the no-bootstrap hot path then resolved to no target.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- `isExternalPluginTarget` now normalizes the raw target via `normalizeMessageChannel` before calling `isDeliverableMessageChannel` and `normalizeChatChannelId`. This mirrors the config validation contract where installed plugin channel ids are lowercased.
- Imported `normalizeMessageChannel` from `../../utils/message-channel.js` alongside the existing `isDeliverableMessageChannel`.

**New regression test** (+1 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ "pre-activates a mixed-case external plugin target" — `target: "Proof-Channel"` is normalized to `proof-channel`, classified as external, and resolved with `allowBootstrap: true`
- Added `normalizeMessageChannel` mock that lowercases input, matching the production contract

**Test results**: 23/23 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (146 total). `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.

target.title: [codex] fix gateway hot-mode restart reloads
target.body:
## Summary

Closes the silent-staleness hole in `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"` without changing the shipped default contract. Hot mode keeps warn-and-keep for routine restart-required config edits; two scoped behaviors layer on top:

- **`gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired: true`** (new optional key, default `false`): opt-in that delegates restart-required edits to the gateway's existing idle-aware restart path, matching `mode: "hybrid"` for the restart-required branch while keeping hot-safe edits hot.
- **Security-critical carve-out** (always on): restart reasons under `gateway.auth.*`, `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, and top-level `secrets.*` schedule a restart even in default hot mode. Without this, a `gateway.auth.token` rotation, a doctor batch that renames `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` profiles, or a `secrets.providers.*` change on disk sits behind warn-and-keep while the runtime keeps honoring the stale credential/profile state.

The hot-mode restart policy is one shared decision (`resolveHotModeRestartDecision`) used by both the file watcher and the `config.patch` / `config.apply` RPC write path, so the two write surfaces cannot diverge. **This changes current RPC behavior in hot mode**: previously `config.patch`/`config.apply` scheduled a direct restart for any restart-required write regardless of the opt-in; now routine restart-required RPC writes return a `requiresRestart` notice without bouncing the gateway (matching the watcher's warn-and-keep contract), while security-critical and opted-in writes still schedule the direct restart.

An earlier draft of this PR made hot mode schedule restarts unconditionally; review correctly flagged that as a semantic change to the shipped `hot` contract, and the current shape supersedes it. Existing `mode: "hot"` deployments are behavior-stable on upgrade for routine edits.

## Details

- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:32`: `SECURITY_CRITICAL_RESTART_PREFIXES = ["gateway.auth", "auth.profiles", "auth.order", "secrets"]`. The `auth.profiles` / `auth.order` entries fix the review-found P1: the production repro (doctor batch renaming `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` with model routes) produced restart reasons under `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, which are unmatched in the reload-plan rules and default to restart-required — so default hot mode dropped them with a warn. The `secrets` prefix is top-level, fixing the earlier `gateway.secrets` prefix that could never match real restart reasons; `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts` marks `secrets.providers.*` restart-required so the carve-out has a live trigger.
- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:54`: `resolveHotModeRestartDecision` returns `"security-critical" | "opt-in" | "warn-and-keep"` and is the single owner of the hot-mode policy.
- `src/gateway/config-reload.ts:319`: the watcher's restart-required hot branch routes through the shared decision; the existing idle-aware restart machinery (`queueRestart`) remains the only watcher restart path.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts:178`: fixes the review-found P2 divergence — `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` now routes hot-mode RPC writes through the same decision instead of unconditionally direct-restarting (`scheduleDirectRestart: mode === "hot"`).
- `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` added to `src/config/types.gateway.ts`, `zod-schema.ts` (strict validation), `schema.help.ts`, `schema.labels.ts`.
- Regression tests pin each branch: warn-and-keep preserved on non-security edits; opt-in queues a supervised restart; security-critical auth/secrets changes restart regardless of the opt-in; the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` rename auto-restarts in default hot mode (`src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`); and the RPC path is pinned three ways in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts:366-421` (routine write keeps running with `requiresRestart: true`, opt-in direct-restarts, auth-token write direct-restarts).
- Docs updated: `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`, `docs/gateway/configuration.md`, `docs/gateway/index.md` describe the default, the opt-in, the carve-out, and that the policy applies to both file edits and `config.patch`/`config.apply` writes.

**Open maintainer decision:** this adds one config key on a compatibility-sensitive surface, and there is no maintainer sign-off yet on the `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` key. The default split (warn-and-keep stays default; auth-profile/auth/secrets changes always restart) is the proposed contract — if a different split is preferred (e.g. opt-in defaulting `true` for fresh installs only), say the word and I will adjust. The RPC alignment above is also a deliberate behavior change to today's hot-mode `config.patch` direct-restart; if maintainers prefer the RPC surface to keep direct-restarting unconditionally, that is a one-line revert in `resolveConfigRestartRequirement`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: in hot reload mode, a config write touching any restart-required key was dropped with a single `log.warn` while the gateway kept serving from the stale in-memory snapshot. Observed in production as a 4-hour silent outage where the agent kept resolving the legacy `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` model id after `openclaw doctor --fix` had migrated the on-disk config (including `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` renames) to `openai/gpt-5.5`; group messages silently dropped, admin DMs returned a canned `[agent failed]` reply. With this patch, security-critical edits (gateway auth, auth profiles/order, secrets) self-heal via restart by default, and operators can opt all restart-required edits into the same path.

- **Real environment tested**: isolated sandbox gateway on macOS (loopback port 28789), dist built from this branch at commit `d023afb9c4` (the commit introducing the opt-in + carve-out design); plus the original production incident capture on a launchd-supervised deployed gateway (`gateway-host`) documenting the pre-fix failure mode. The subsequent changes (top-level `secrets` prefix, `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` prefixes, shared RPC policy, rebase onto current main) are pinned by focused regression tests run locally at head `074e8acf36`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: sandbox scenarios (at `d023afb9c4`): start a fresh sandbox gateway from the branch dist, wait for the config watcher to settle, write one config edit, observe the reload log and process state.
  ```
  Scenario A: mode "hot" (defaults), edit gateway.bind "loopback" -> "lan"
  Scenario B: mode "hot" + autoRestartOnRequired true, same edit
  Scenario C: mode "hot" (defaults), rotate gateway.auth.token
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36`:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: redacted runtime log captured live from the sandbox gateway reload/restart console output (at `d023afb9c4`):
  ```
  A: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.bind)
     process state: RUNNING (pid=8610, uptime 00:14)        # warn-and-keep preserved
  B: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart per gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired=true (gateway.bind)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     [shutdown] started: gateway restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=6706, uptime 00:15)        # restarted clean
  C: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart for security-critical change (gateway.auth.token)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=9261, uptime 00:14)        # credential rotation propagated
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36` (local, macOS, Node 24):
  ```
  Test Files  8 passed (8)
       Tests  474 passed (474)
  ```
  including the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` watcher regression and the three hot-mode `config.patch` policy tests. `tsgo` core + core-test lanes and `oxfmt`/`oxlint` on touched files also pass.

- **Observed result after fix**: scenario A proves existing hot-mode deployments keep the shipped warn-and-keep contract with no restart. Scenario B proves the opt-in routes routine restart-required edits through the existing SIGUSR1 + clean-shutdown restart path. Scenario C proves auth rotations propagate by default, closing the credential-rotation-bypass gap. The production failure mode (`hot mode ignoring` on `auth.profiles.*` for 4 hours) is now closed at the exact prefix that caused it, pinned by the regression test at `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`.

- **What was not tested**: live sandbox-gateway captures were not re-run at the final head — the `secrets.providers.*` rotation and the doctor-batch `auth.profiles` rename scenarios are proven at head `074e8acf36` by focused regression tests only, not by a fresh end-to-end gateway capture; this is a known proof gap called out for review. Also untested: launchd auto-respawn end-to-end on hosts using `KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }` (see operator note below — the clean-exit hand-off needs a kickstart watcher on such hosts; not a regression, the pre-fix path also required manual intervention). The sandbox ran unmanaged (in-process restart mode); the managed-install launchd restart path is covered by existing integration tests.

## Operator note: launchd `SuccessfulExit=false` hosts

Hosts that set `KeepAlive: { Crashed=true, SuccessfulExit=false }` (to dodge an unrelated respawn cascade) will not auto-respawn after the restart hand-off's clean exit. The deployment fork pairs this with a 30s interval watchdog (`launchctl print` state AND port-binding check, then `launchctl kickstart -k`) — documented here so the gap flagged in review is paired with its operational answer. Hosts on default launchd `KeepAlive` semantics respawn normally and need nothing.

target.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw had local backup export/verify, but no low-friction folder-backed snapshot flow for encrypted backups plus workspace mirroring.
- Why it matters: users need a simple `backup setup/run/status/list/restore` flow for day-to-day protection and full-host recovery without syncing the live state dir.
- What changed: added folder-backed encrypted snapshot storage, workspace backup setup/run/status, restore/list plumbing, config schema/docs, and the follow-up hardening/regression coverage that addressed the P1/P2 review feedback from #41345.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not add provider-specific cloud APIs, device-identity export/import, or any live state-dir sync behavior.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #32921
- Related #40090
- Related #7598
- Related #41345

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Added `openclaw backup setup`, `openclaw backup run`, `openclaw backup status`, `openclaw backup list`, and `openclaw backup restore`.
- `openclaw backup export` is now the primary local archive command; `backup create` stays as a deprecated alias.
- `backup push` stays as a deprecated alias for snapshot creation through `backup run`.
- `reset` and `uninstall` now recommend `openclaw backup export`.
- Backup config now supports `backup.target` and `backup.encryption.key` for folder-backed encrypted snapshots.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - Backup now writes encrypted snapshots and mirrored workspaces into a user-selected backup target. Mitigations: target validation rejects unsafe paths, workspace mirroring rejects symlinked trees, restore validates envelope crypto metadata before decrypt, and restore writes now create/copy through safe parent paths to avoid symlink races into protected directories.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / pnpm workspace
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): `backup.target=<temp dir>`, `backup.encryption.key=<redacted>`

### Steps

1. Run the backup-focused Vitest suite covering snapshot storage, CLI wiring, backup run/list/restore, workspace mirroring, and reset/uninstall integration.
2. Run `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` on the rebased branch.
3. Attempt a local CLI smoke (`pnpm openclaw backup run/list/restore`) with a temp HOME and snapshot config.

### Expected

- Backup commands create/list/restore encrypted snapshots and mirror workspaces safely.
- Build/check pass unless blocked by unrelated main-branch issues.
- Local CLI smoke exercises the new flow end-to-end.

### Actual

- The backup-focused Vitest suite passed.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, and the local CLI smoke are currently blocked by unrelated `main` breakage after rebasing: `@mariozechner/pi-ai` no longer exports `getOAuthApiKey`, `getOAuthProviders`, or `loginOpenAICodex`, which breaks `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts`, `src/commands/openai-codex-oauth.ts`, and several agent wrapper files before backup code runs.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Commands run:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/backup.test.ts src/commands/backup-run.test.ts src/commands/backup-verify.test.ts src/commands/backup-status.test.ts src/commands/backup-snapshot.test.ts src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts src/commands/workspace-backup.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/config.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/encryption.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/provider-folder.test.ts src/backup/snapshot-store/targets.test.ts src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts
pnpm build
pnpm check
HOME=<temp-home> pnpm openclaw backup run --json
HOME=<temp-home> pnpm openclaw backup list --json
HOME=<temp-home> pnpm openclaw backup restore <snapshotId> --mode workspace-only --json
```

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: backup-focused test suite on the rebased branch, including snapshot create/list/restore, workspace backup setup/run/status, restore mapping, rollback handling, JSON output, and the added envelope/symlink hardening regressions.
- Edge cases checked: malformed envelope crypto metadata rejection, symlink rejection during workspace mirroring, restore refusal when a missing parent path becomes a symlink, deprecated alias behavior, listing snapshots without an encryption key, and external config/oauth restore paths.
- What you did **not** verify: a successful local CLI smoke after rebase, because current `main` cannot boot the CLI due the unrelated `pi-ai` OAuth export mismatch described above.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:
  - Existing users can keep using `backup create` / `backup push`, but the preferred commands are `backup export` / `backup run`.
  - To enable encrypted snapshots, set `backup.target` and `backup.encryption.key`.

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: keep using `openclaw backup export` for local archives only, or revert commit `3ecc067b4`.
- Files/config to restore: `openclaw.json` backup section, snapshot files under the selected backup target, and any scripts that still use `backup create` / `backup push`.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: `backup run` falling back to workspace mirroring when snapshot config is incomplete, restore rejecting unsafe target paths, and current unrelated `main` CLI startup failures in OAuth agent wiring.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: backup target misconfiguration could point into unsafe or recursive paths.
  - Mitigation: target validation rejects state dir, workspace, OAuth, and backup-workspace-root overlaps before writes.
- Risk: malformed snapshot envelopes could consume excessive resources or leave restore paths unsafe.
  - Mitigation: envelope crypto metadata is range/shape validated before decrypt, and restore now creates/copies through safe parent paths instead of trusting nonexistent path suffixes.
- Risk: alias compatibility could drift from the primary commands.
  - Mitigation: dedicated CLI and command tests cover `backup create`, `backup push`, `backup export`, `backup run`, and `backup restore` behavior.

target.title: fix: gate Gateway message action requester provenance [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a write-scoped Gateway client could provide requester identity fields on `message.action` requests and have that identity treated as trusted channel provenance by downstream message actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now treats requester account and sender provenance like other trusted channel-action context: only full-scope callers can bridge server-injected requester identity through the public RPC boundary. Write-scoped clients can still invoke supported message actions, but their caller-supplied requester identity and owner bit are stripped before channel dispatch.

## User Impact

Operators keep the existing `message.action` workflow for normal write-scoped clients, while channel actions that depend on trusted sender identity no longer accept spoofed requester provenance from those clients. This narrows the authorization boundary without changing channel configuration, storage, migrations, or plugin manifests.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted PR.
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` passed: 124 tests.
- Remote validation attempted first, but unavailable in this environment: Blacksmith Testbox requires a newer Crabbox binary, direct AWS broker login is missing, and `blacksmith` CLI is unavailable.
