target.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock
target.body:
## Summary

A long-running gateway can permanently deadlock its entire agent lane on a stuck OAuth auth-refresh. The runtime auth single-flight in `auth-controller.ts` stores the in-flight refresh promise in `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight`; every model turn that needs auth does `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` **with no timeout**. If the underlying provider auth hook (`prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` -> OAuth refresh, keychain read, or cross-agent file-lock wait) never settles, `refreshInFlight` is never cleared and **every subsequent turn hangs forever** awaiting it. The process stays alive and the port stays open, so it looks healthy while no replies are produced.

Observed in production: a gateway froze mid-day right after a token hit expiry. Process alive (11d uptime, port listening) but fully idle since the freeze, zero sockets to the provider, all threads parked, one never-resolving `await`. On-disk token was valid the whole time (a fresh process pre-warmed auth in ~0.7s), and no on-disk lock was held — i.e. a pure in-memory single-flight deadlock.

This adds a hard deadline so the single-flight promise **always** settles:

- New `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline()` + `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (300s) in `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`. 300s sits above the OAuth manager's own 120s call timeout plus a peer's 180s stale-lock window, so a legitimately slow cross-agent refresh still completes while a true hang is forced to reject.
- `refreshRuntimeAuth` wraps the refresh operation in that deadline; on timeout it rejects, the `.finally` clears `refreshInFlight`, and all waiters unblock with a descriptive error instead of hanging.
- The `.finally` clear is no longer gated on `generation`: a profile rotation during a slow/hung refresh must still release the handle it owns, otherwise a stale handle wedges the new generation. The existing `refreshInFlight === refreshPromise` identity guard still prevents clobbering a newer refresh.

No behavior change on the happy path (fast refresh resolves long before the deadline). The deadline is a backstop only.

## Repro / Test plan

- [x] `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline` unit tests: rejects after the deadline when work never settles (fake timers), resolves/propagates when work wins the race, passes through unbounded for non-positive timeout, and the default exceeds the OAuth call + stale-lock budget.
- [x] `auth-controller` regression test: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever sets `refreshInFlight`, then after advancing past the hard deadline the wedged handle rejects with `exceeded hard deadline` and is no longer the active in-flight handle.
- [x] Proof the test catches the bug: with the deadline neutralized (timeout `0` = unbounded), the regression test **times out / FAILS**; restored, it passes.
- [x] Current-head scoped run: see Evidence below.

Thanks @amittell.

---

## Update: complete the deadlock class (not just the refresh path)

A follow-up audit found the original commit only backstopped ONE of several entry paths into the same auth lock/gate machinery. Both remaining paths could still permanently wedge the agent lane the same way:

1. **Cold-start / profile-rotation path (critical).** `applyApiKeyInfo` (the path `initializeAuthProfile` and `advanceAuthProfile` use, and the first turn a watchdog restart lands on) awaited `resolveApiKeyForCandidate` and `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` — the exact hook that hung in production — with no deadline. A single shared local `withAuthDeadline` helper now wraps every auth boundary in `auth-controller.ts` (refresh AND cold-start), so a hung provider hook fails the turn over instead of deadlocking the lane.
2. **In-lock keychain / buildApiKey (high).** In `oauth-manager.ts`, `withRefreshCallTimeout` wrapped only the network refresh call; the in-lock keychain store load and `buildApiKey` ran un-deadlined while the cross-agent file lock was held, so a wedged keychain pinned the lock and chain-stalled every same-key refresher behind the un-timed `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh gate (`refreshQueue.enqueue` chains each caller on the previous tail with no timeout). The whole held-lock critical section is now bounded by `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (150s), kept strictly between the 120s call timeout and the 180s stale window.

### Added proof
- `auth-controller` cold-start regression test: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever on `initializeAuthProfile` now fails over within the deadline; **neutralizing the backstop makes the test time out / FAIL** (deadlock reproduced), confirming it catches the bug.
- `oauth-manager` invariant test pins `OAUTH_REFRESH_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS < OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS < stale`.
- All touched suites green at the current head; see Evidence below.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Current `main` still awaits `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` in `auth-controller.ts` with no timeout, and the `.finally` clear is generation-gated, so one provider auth hook, keychain read, or cross-agent lock wait that never settles leaves the in-flight handle pending forever and every later model turn deadlocks awaiting it. The gateway process stays alive and its port stays open, so monitoring sees a healthy process while the agent lane produces no replies until a manual restart. This PR makes every runtime auth boundary settle: a hard 300s deadline on the single-flight refresh and cold-start paths, an ungated in-flight-handle clear, and a 150s bound on the whole held-lock OAuth critical section so a wedged keychain or hook cannot pin the cross-agent lock and chain-stall every same-key refresher queued behind it.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` at 22376d80e163. The only conflict was `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.ts`; it was resolved by keeping main's current `doRefreshOAuthTokenWithLock` body (the `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh queue from #99691, the refresh-contention error classification from #101573, and `readBootstrapCredential({ store, ... })`) and re-applying only the `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` whole-section wrap on top.

Scoped test run at head ff8c5fea5a3700fcaff387ca66b7959ce148d8da:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
```

Sibling auth suites also pass at the same head: `oauth-refresh-queue`, `oauth-refresh-timeout`, `oauth-lock-timeout-classification`, `oauth-refresh-failure`, `oauth.concurrent-agents`, `oauth`, `oauth.fallback-to-main-agent`, `oauth.adopt-identity`, and `oauth.mirror-refresh` test files all green via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ...` (2 Vitest shards passed). `tsgo` core lane exits 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all seven changed files.

Production soak on a fork: gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06, and the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: gateway agent lane permanently deadlocks when one runtime auth refresh never settles; every later model turn hangs on an un-timed `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` while the process looks healthy.
Real environment tested: production gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06; the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts
Evidence after fix: 3 test files, 39 tests passed at head ff8c5fea5a3700fcaff387ca66b7959ce148d8da, including the hang-regression tests that time out and fail when the deadline backstop is neutralized; nine sibling oauth lock/queue/refresh test files also pass at the same head.
Observed result after fix: a hung provider auth hook or in-lock keychain wait now rejects at the deadline, the in-flight handle is cleared, waiting turns fail over with a descriptive error instead of deadlocking, and the production fork gateways have had no recurrence of the freeze.
What was not tested: live upstream-main gateway soak at this exact head; full build and broad CI lanes are left to PR CI.

target.title: Dashboard: stream + computed data-binding kinds
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** bind a widget with `stream:` or `computed:` → the stream comes from the allowlisted gateway events; `computed` is a fixed op set with **no eval**.

---


> Live push feeds and derived values, not just files: bind a widget to a gateway event stream, or compute one from other bindings — safely, with no new network and no expression language.

Closes #101150. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `schema.ts` / `index.ts` / `data-read.ts` deltas.

## What's in this PR
Two new binding kinds alongside the existing `file` / `static` / `rpc`:
- **`stream`** — push updates from an **allowlisted** gateway broadcast channel. It does **not** open a socket: it multiplexes over the Control UI's existing gateway WebSocket via `client.addEventListener`, and the event id must be one of a small `STREAM_EVENT_ALLOWLIST` (`presence`, `sessions.changed`, `plugin.dashboard.changed` — all read-only). Enforced at write time in the schema *and* re-checked at subscribe time (defense-in-depth), so a stream binding can never listen on an arbitrary channel. Unsubscribes on unmount.
- **`computed`** — a value derived from the resolved values of *sibling* bindings via exactly one **fixed, whitelisted op**: `sum · avg · min · max · count · last · pick(pointer) · format(template)`. It's a `switch` — **no expression language, no `eval`, no `Function`**. `pick` is a read-only pointer traversal; `format` interpolates resolved values into a bounded template.

**Deliberately excluded:** a `command:` binding (running shell commands) is *not* here — arbitrary command execution deserves its own security-reviewed PR, so it's carved out.

## How it works & why it's safe
`resolveBinding` gains branches on both sides (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/index.ts` client, `extensions/dashboard/src/data-read.ts` server returns a typed client-resolved marker like `rpc` does), and the schema union validates both kinds strictly. Two structural safety properties:
- **No arbitrary network** — `stream` is an allowlist over already-published gateway events on the existing socket; there is no code path to an external URL.
- **No cycles, no code exec** — a `computed` input may only reference a *non-computed* binding, which makes a reference cycle structurally impossible (no graph walk needed); and the op set is a closed switch, so there's no evaluator to exploit.

No new dependency.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bindings were limited to `file` / `static` / `rpc` — no way to push-update a widget from a live event or derive a value from other bindings without polling. This adds `stream` (allowlisted gateway events, multiplexed over the existing socket) and `computed` (fixed op set), with `command:` deliberately deferred to its own reviewed PR.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm -C ui vitest run src/lib/dashboard` green — schema accept/reject for both kinds (unknown op, malformed inputs, non-allowlisted event, computed→computed rejection), each computed op's result, and stream subscribe→push→unsubscribe over a mocked event source; `pnpm ui:i18n:check`, `pnpm ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean. Counts confirmed by the submitting orchestrator's own gate run.

target.title: Dashboard: control hub — per-agent nesting, shared/private tabs, presence
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** with ≥2 agents/operators — group the tab strip by agent, mark a tab **private**, and watch presence → a private tab is **absent server-side** from a non-owner's payload (fail-closed); live "who's viewing" presence.

---

# Dashboard: control hub — per-agent nesting, shared/private tabs, presence

> The multi-agent, multi-operator half of the vision: organize the dashboard by which agent built what, keep some tabs private, and see who else is in the workspace live.

Closes #101151, #101152, #101153. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff.

## What's in this PR
- **Per-agent nesting (#101151)** — group the tab strip by each tab's `createdBy` provenance, with a collapse/expand control to fold a whole agent's tabs away. Pure grouping over existing provenance.
- **Shared/private tabs (#101152)** — a tab may be `private`, visible only to its owner (enforced server-side, below).
- **Presence (#101153)** — a lightweight "who's viewing this tab" indicator over the existing broadcast path; the presence event carries `{ operator, tabSlug, at }` (id + tab only, never document state), ephemeral and never persisted.

## Security (private tabs)
Visibility is enforced **server-side**, not by hiding in the UI: every gateway response that serializes the workspace doc passes through `filterWorkspaceForOperator(doc, resolveOperatorIdentity(client))` (a `respondDoc` helper on `workspace.get`, every mutation response, `tab.create`, and `undo`), so a private tab the caller doesn't own is absent from the wire payload **and** the tab order. The store keeps the full doc; only the response is filtered. **Fail-closed:** an unidentified operator sees zero private tabs. (Operator identity is currently keyed on the paired **device id** — documented as the exact seam where a richer per-human identity threads in; a bootstrap-authed connection with no paired device can neither see nor own a private tab.)

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** With many agents and/or operators sharing one dashboard, there was no way to organize by agent, keep a tab private, or see concurrent activity. This adds per-agent grouping, server-enforced private tabs, and live presence.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 90 passed (visibility filter, fail-closed default, owner-only access, presence-payload shape — a private tab owned by A verified absent from B's serialized payload and tab order); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` → 119 passed (actor grouping/fold, presence store TTL + self-exclusion, visibility round-trip); `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean.

target.title: Dashboard: apps layer — full-bleed tabs + widget gallery
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** toggle a tab to full-bleed and open the widget gallery → a full-bleed "tab app"; gallery install-from-URL routes through the L5 approval gate (no auto-mount).

---

# Dashboard: apps layer — full-bleed tabs + widget gallery

> Two steps toward "every tab is a web app": a tab can be a single full-bleed widget, and widgets can be browsed and installed from a registry — through the same approval gate and sandbox as any custom widget.

Closes #101148 and #101149. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the full-bleed layout + gallery pieces as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **Full-bleed tab (#101148)** — a tab may set `layout: "full"`, rendering a single widget filling the content area with no grid chrome; a menu toggle flips it. A custom widget can now *be* the tab — a real app surface.
- **Widget gallery + install-from-URL (#101149)** — browse a registry `index.json`, see the capabilities a widget requests, and install it. The **browser** fetches the index + bundle and sends only the fetched `{ name, manifest, files }` to a new `dashboard.widget.install` method (512 KB / 64-file caps).

## Security (gallery)
The gallery is the third-party-code surface, so it's deliberately conservative: **install is client-fetch only** — the gateway never receives or fetches a URL (a source-scan guard test asserts no `fetch`/`https` in the install path), so there is no server-side SSRF; the bundle is capped (512 KB, ≤64 files), path-jailed, extension-allowlisted, and run through the existing `validateWidgetManifest`; requested capabilities are surfaced *before* install. Installing never auto-approves and never bypasses the sandbox — an installed widget lands `pending`, passes the existing operator-approval gate (#101098), and runs in the same `allow-scripts`, opaque-origin, `connect-src 'none'` iframe as any custom widget.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard couldn't express a full app-per-tab, and there was no supply side for widgets (everything hand-authored). This adds a full-bleed tab layout and an approval-gated, sandboxed install-from-registry path.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 92 passed (install caps, path jail, `pending` status, and a no-server-fetch source guard); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin src/components` → 299 passed (gallery client-fetch + install, full-bleed render/toggle); `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, and full type-aware oxlint clean. The 3 failures in the full suite are the pre-existing `terminal-panel` browser-fixture flake, unrelated to this change.

> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map). > > 🧪 **Try this PR:** add a `builtin:action-form` (`template: "Deploy {env}"`) and submit → it dispatches through the **same** operator-confirm + rate gate as the sandbox bridge; `ephemeral` answer-widgets self-sweep; **Pin** makes one permanent. --- # Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop > Two halves of the flagship interaction: the agent answers show-don't-tell questions by composing a live widget, and widgets can act — a button or form that dispatches a parameterized prompt back to the agent. Closes #101820 and #101821. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `action-form`, `ephemeral`, and Living-Answers pieces as the delta. ## What's in this PR - **`ephemeral` + pin (#101820)** — a widget may carry `ephemeral: { expiresAt }`; the store sweeps expired ephemeral widgets on read (one atomic write, only when something expired, version bumped), and a **Pin** action in the cell menu clears the marker to make it permanent. So an agent can answer with a self-cleaning widget on an "Answers" tab; a useful answer is one click from permanent. - **`builtin:action-form` (#101821)** — an operator-authored button/form whose fields interpolate into a `template` and submit dispatches it back to the agent. "Deploy {env}", "Triage {id} as {priority}" become one-click playbooks. - **Living-Answers convention** — an agent-facing doc (`extensions/dashboard/docs/LIVING-ANSWERS.md`) + 3 worked examples: answer visual questions with a live widget, not prose. ## Security (action-form) - **No new dispatch privilege.** Submit routes through `dispatchRateLimitedPrompt` — the *exact same* operator-confirm + rate-limit gate the sandboxed custom-widget bridge's `sendPrompt` uses. A test proves an action-form and a same-keyed bridge share one exhausted rate budget. - **No template injection.** Interpolation is a single pass over the *authored template* with a function replacer: each `{slot}` resolves to its declared field's typed, length-capped value (default 200/field), and the inserted text is never re-scanned — an injected `{evil}` inside a field value stays literal (tested). The template is authored into the workspace document (operator-approvable, schema-validated: ≤2000 chars, ≤8 fields, every `{slot}` must name a declared field). ## How it works **Dispatch flow — one shared gate, single-pass interpolation (the security argument, visual):** ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as action-form widget participant P as Dashboard parent participant G as dispatchRateLimitedPrompt (shared gate) participant Chat as Agent / chat W->>P: submit { field values } P->>P: single-pass interpolate the AUTHORED template
{slot} → typed, length-capped field · result never re-scanned P->>G: dispatch(prompt) G->>G: operator-confirm dialog + rate-limit
(same budget as the sandbox bridge's sendPrompt — no new privilege) G->>Chat: prompt (only if confirmed AND under budget) ``` The `ephemeral` marker is a tiny schema addition swept in the store's existing read path; `action-form` is a trusted builtin registered like the others; the dispatch gate was extracted (`dispatchRateLimitedPrompt`) so the builtin and the sandbox bridge share one code path. No new dependency; no new gateway privilege. Note: this builds on the corrected base (#101098) where the UI↔gateway widget-mutation and file-binding contracts were fixed — pin uses the corrected `{ tab, id, patch }` mutation contract. ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard could show data but not *act*, and agent answers to visual questions were prose that died in the transcript. This adds the acting half (an action-form widget that dispatches through the existing gate) and the answering convention (ephemeral answer-widgets + pin). **Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` green — schema validation (template/field caps, unknown-slot reject, ISO ephemeral), the store TTL sweep, the single-pass no-double-expansion interpolation, and the shared-rate-budget dispatch; `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full oxlint clean. target.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown
target.body:
## Summary

On rh-bot.lan at 2026-05-31 21:31 a gateway PID (71842) logged `[shutdown] completed cleanly in 5ms`, but the node process never exited. It held port 18789 for 2h13m. Every subsequent launchd-spawned gateway then took the lock-recovery path: probe `/healthz`, see 200 from the zombie, log `gateway already running under launchd; existing gateway is healthy, leaving it in control`, and exit 0. launchd's `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false` kept new gateways down. The bot was offline for about 2h13m until manual `kill -9` plus `launchctl kickstart -k`.

The original SIGKILL of the parent process is the separate root cause documented in memory `project_rh_bot_isolated_session_sigkill.md` (`openclaw isolated-session` spawn pattern). This PR fixes the second-order defenses that should have prevented the zombie from blocking restart, not the SIGKILL itself.

## Layer 1: force exit after every clean shutdown

`src/gateway/server-close.ts:738` already logs `shutdown completed cleanly in Xms`, but a stray handle (HTTP keep-alive, telegram fetch, plugin native handle) can keep the event loop alive after every owned subsystem closed. `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts:382` has an existing `armForceExitTimer(SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS)` safety net, but it only arms for `runAcceptedRequest` (signal-driven), not for the `closeOnStartupFailure` path in `src/gateway/server.impl.ts:1059`. That gap is exactly the rh-bot incident shape.

This PR adds `armGatewayPostShutdownExitWatchdog` in `server-close.ts`. After "completed cleanly" is logged, an unref'd `setTimeout` is armed (default 5_000ms, configurable via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_POST_SHUTDOWN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS`). When it fires:
- emit a structured `shutdownLog.warn` with the active-handle constructor summary (via `process._getActiveHandles` or `getActiveResourcesInfo`)
- record the `gateway.shutdown.zombie_detected` restart trace event for OTel/Loki
- call `process.exit(0)`

Because the timer is unref'd, a healthy natural exit always wins. The watchdog only fires when something else holds the loop open. The injected callback shape (`armPostShutdownExitWatchdog` parameter on `createGatewayCloseHandler`) keeps vitest workers from killing themselves during the suite.

## Layer 2: 503 on /healthz during shutdown, plus tighter preflight

The deployed `handleGatewayProbeRequest` in `src/gateway/server-http.ts` returns 200 unconditionally for `/healthz`. A zombie still holding its HTTP listener therefore answers 200, and `probeGatewayHealthz` in `src/cli/gateway-cli/run.ts:369` accepts it as healthy (success criterion was `statusCode < 500`). The lock-recovery loop then logs `gateway already running under launchd; existing gateway is healthy, leaving it in control` and returns void to the supervisor, which respawns nothing.

This PR adds a module-level shutting-down flag in `server-close.ts`, flipped to `shutting_down` at the start of the close handler (before any await). `handleGatewayProbeRequest` consults that flag via injectable `getShuttingDown` accessor (defaults to `isGatewayShuttingDown`). When live probes (`/health`, `/healthz`) run while shutting down, they return 503 with body `{ "live": false, "phase": "shutting_down" }`. A `gateway.healthz.shutting_down_response` warn log fires once per shutdown sequence so the cascade is queryable in Loki without spamming.

`probeGatewayHealthz` is tightened to accept only `statusCode === 200`. The previous `< 500` admitted the new 503 (and any 4xx misconfig), defeating the layer 2 purpose. The lock-recovery loop now also emits `gateway.preflight.zombie_detected` (warn log plus restart trace event) when the lock is held but the probe is unhealthy, so subsequent supervisor cycles can be correlated.

The flag resets at the start of `startGatewayServer` so the in-process restart path returns to a `running` state before `/healthz` starts answering 200 again.

## OTel / Loki instrumentation

All four events emit via the existing `gatewayLog`/`shutdownLog`/`gatewayProbeLog` subsystems plus `recordGatewayRestartTrace`:

- `gateway.shutdown.zombie_detected` (Layer 1 trace) when the post-shutdown watchdog fires
- `gateway.healthz.shutting_down_response` (Layer 2 warn log) when /healthz returns 503 during shutdown
- `gateway.preflight.zombie_detected` (Layer 2 warn log + trace) when supervised lock recovery sees a held lock but an unhealthy probe
- the existing `restart.close.total` trace already covers clean-path shutdown completion

No new export plumbing is needed; the existing diagnostics-otel / Loki shipper consumes these events.

## Verification

Local Vitest with the patch applied:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-close.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.probe.test.ts src/gateway/probe.close-drain.test.ts src/gateway/server.preauth-hardening.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run.supervised-lock.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  59 passed (59)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  10 passed (10)
```

`pnpm build` clean. `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --only=core --threads=4` clean. `node scripts/check-dynamic-import-warts.mjs` shows only the pre-existing `mcp-cli.ts` advisory, unchanged by this PR.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: gateway zombie shutdown that left rh-bot offline 2h13m on 2026-05-31. With this PR the watchdog forces `process.exit(0)` so launchd reaps the PID, and `/healthz` returns 503 during shutdown so the next supervisor cycle does not defer to a draining instance.

Real environment tested: live deployed openclaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, build SHA 23804e610c (incident reproducer). The deployed bundle is the exact code that exhibited the bug; the proof script exercises both the deployed predicate and the patched predicate against real HTTP servers, plus the watchdog state machine.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
scp /tmp/proof-zombie-amittell.mjs alexm@rh-bot.lan:/tmp/proof-zombie-amittell.mjs
ssh alexm@rh-bot.lan 'cd /tmp && node proof-zombie-amittell.mjs'
ssh alexm@rh-bot.lan 'curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz'
```

Evidence after fix:

```
== gateway zombie-shutdown fix proof ==
host: rh-bot.lan
node: v25.8.2
date: 2026-06-01T04:28:32.289Z

[PASS] case1 deployed handler returns 200 mid-shutdown so old preflight defers to zombie :: accepted=true
[PASS] case2 patched predicate (=== 200) rejects 503 as unhealthy :: accepted=false
[PASS] case3 patched predicate accepts a healthy 200 response :: accepted=true
[PASS] case4 watchdog calls exitProcess(0) after timeout :: exited=true; warnMessages=1
[PASS] case4 watchdog warn log names the timeout in ms :: gateway shutdown completed but node process still alive after 50ms; forcing process.exit(0)
[PASS] case5 cancelling the watchdog prevents the forced exit :: exited=false
[PASS] case6a healthz returns 200 ok:true when running :: {"statusCode":200,"body":{"ok":true,"status":"live"}}
[PASS] case6b healthz returns 503 live:false phase:shutting_down when shutdown started :: {"statusCode":503,"body":{"live":false,"phase":"shutting_down"}}

PROOF SUMMARY  passed=8  failed=0
```

Live deployed gateway healthz hit (confirms the case 1 handler shape the proof script reproduces):

```
$ curl -s -w "status=%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz
status=200
{"ok":true,"status":"live"}
```

Observed result after fix: case 1 confirms the deployed handler shape responsible for the incident. Cases 2 and 3 confirm the patched probe predicate. Cases 4 and 5 confirm the watchdog forces exit on the deployed Node runtime and stops cleanly when cancelled. Cases 6a and 6b confirm the healthz state machine returns the canonical 200 ok body when running and the 503 `{ live: false, phase: "shutting_down" }` body the moment the shutdown flag is set.

What was not tested: a true end-to-end shutdown of a real OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot with the new bundle (requires deployment of this branch); the long-running TCP keepalive vs telegram-fetch handle-leak scenario, which the watchdog handles by design (any stray handle keeps the loop alive past the watchdog timeout, and the watchdog forces exit regardless of the specific handle source).

target.title: Dashboard: ops widgets — agent status + approvals queue
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** add the `agent-status` + `approvals` builtins → live agent activity, and an approvals queue you can action from the dashboard.

---

> The operational half of the builtin set: see what every agent is doing, and act on what's waiting for you — from a dashboard cell.

Closes #101145 and #101144. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `agent-status.ts` + `approvals.ts` and their wiring as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**`builtin:agent-status` (#101145)** — a compact per-agent/session status list: active-run vs idle, current label, and freshness — the "what's everything doing right now?" glance. It binds to the same `sessions.list` data the `sessions` builtin already uses (no new backend), so it live-updates on the existing broadcast path.

**`builtin:approvals` (#101144)** — a pending-approvals queue with Approve/Deny actions, wired end-to-end through the **existing** widget-approval infrastructure from #101098 (`dashboard.widget.approve`): pending `custom:` widgets appear as cards, and a decision dispatches the same client path the Workspaces pending-card uses. The queue arrives via a new `ctx.approvals` source on the builtin context (mirroring the existing `ctx.embed` pattern), because it's in-memory workspace state rather than an RPC binding.

**Scope note (deliberate):** the gateway's exec/plugin approval RPCs (`exec.approval.*`, `plugin.approval.*`) exist and the app shell uses them, but they are operator-scoped and not in the dashboard's read-only binding allowlist (`DATA_READ_RPC_ALLOWLIST`). Widening that allowlist is a security decision we didn't want to smuggle into a widget PR — so this widget covers the dashboard's own approval queue today, and is shaped to take exec/plugin approvals as additional sources the moment maintainers bless that allowlist addition (called out in the module header). That keeps #72545 progressing without expanding any privilege surface.

## How it works
Both widgets follow the established builtin contract (`renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult`), registered in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` + `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN`. Agent-status is a pure mapper over the resolved `sessions.list` value. Approvals renders from `ctx.approvals` (built by the dashboard view from workspace state) and dispatches decisions through the existing, already-authorized `dashboard.widget.approve` method — this PR adds **no new gateway method and no new privilege**.

No new dependency — `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** There's no cross-agent activity view in the dashboard (#101145 / the #39127–#54577 cluster), and approvals had no dashboard surface (#101144, advancing #72545) — operators had to open each session or wait for the pending-card to appear on the Workspaces tab. This adds two operational builtins: a live agent-status list and an approvals queue with working Approve/Deny.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 100 passed, including the new suites (status derivation filters + provenance, decision-vocabulary mapping + limit, populated/empty renders, and Approve/Deny wiring asserted against a mocked client dispatching `dashboard.widget.approve`); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and full type-aware oxlint clean; `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` green (schema kind additions).

target.title: Dashboard: chart widgets + widget authoring SDK
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** add a `builtin:chart` widget (`type: line|bar|area|sparkline|gauge`) bound to a numeric series → a dependency-free SVG chart. Author your own via `docs/plugins/dashboard-widget-authoring.md` + the starter templates.

---

> Two things that make the widget system easier to *use* and easier to *extend*: a family of dependency-free chart widgets, and a guide + starter templates for authoring your own.

Closes #101142 and #101141. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the new `chart.ts` + `docs/`/`examples/` files as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**Chart widgets (#101142)** — a `builtin:chart` renderer covering five visual types via `props.type`: `line`, `bar`, `area`, `sparkline`, `gauge`.
- Rendered as **dependency-free inline SVG** (lit's `svg` template — no charting library, no new npm dependency).
- Binds to a timeseries `value` through the same binding path every builtin uses; the value shape is tolerant (`number[]`, `{x?, y|value}[]`, or `{points:[…]}`) and normalized to a finite `number[]` before drawing.
- Compact, axis-light visuals that scale to the grid cell; empty/missing data falls back to the shared placeholder; `role="img"` + `aria-label`.

**Widget authoring SDK (#101141)** — `docs/plugins/dashboard-widget-authoring.md` plus three copy-paste starter widgets under `extensions/dashboard/examples/widgets/`.
- The guide documents **both** widget paths: builtin renderers (the `renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult` contract, and registering a kind in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` *and* `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN` — which must change together), and sandboxed custom widgets (the `widget.json` manifest, the postMessage bridge, the approval flow, and the CSP/opaque-origin constraints).
- Starter templates: `hello-data` (reads a binding), `notes` (persists via `getState`/`setState`), and `calculator` (self-contained).

## How it works
The chart widget is a pure renderer: it normalizes the resolved binding value to a numeric series, computes a fixed `100×40` viewBox with padded scaling (flat-lining a zero-range series), and emits `polyline` / `polygon` / `rect` / arc `path` elements per type — the gauge is a 180° arc with a needle at the value's position in `[min,max]`. Nothing fetches; the renderer only draws what its binding resolved. The SDK is documentation + example assets only — no runtime code changes.

Note: the SDK guide's `state:persist` capability and `getState`/`setState` bridge messages (used by the `notes` template) are delivered by the write-back PR (#101137 / #101329); the guide documents them as part of the widget system.

This PR adds **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard had only stat-card and table builtins (no way to visualize a trend), and no documented path for contributors or agents to author new widgets. This adds a dependency-free chart widget family and an authoring guide + starter templates for both the builtin and sandboxed-custom widget paths.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → the UI dashboard suite is green (incl. the chart mapping/render suite: normalize shapes, per-type element counts for line/bar/area/gauge, and empty-state); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and oxlint clean. The chart renders only inside a live dashboard grid with a resolved binding, so it's verified via the render tests per repo idiom.

target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** add a `builtin:preview` widget bound to a URL and reload → the live embed renders in the sandbox; the reload/verify controls work.

---

> A live preview panel in the dashboard: embed a running dev server or a deployed URL, with reload and device-frame controls.

Closes #101138 (phase 1). **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the new `preview` widget files as the delta.

## What problem this solves
Operators and maintainers have asked for a browser/preview panel in the dashboard for a long time (#27574). This delivers phase 1: a trusted `builtin:preview` widget that renders a URL inside the same sandboxed embed frame the dashboard already uses, with reload + viewport controls — so a preview is just another widget an agent or human can place.

## What's in this PR
- A new `builtin:preview` widget (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/widgets/preview.ts`) cloned from `iframe-embed`, reusing its sandbox + external-URL policy unchanged.
- Chrome: a reload control, and desktop / tablet / mobile viewport presets that constrain the frame width (default via a widget prop).
- Registered in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS`; `preview` added to `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN`.
- Unit tests: renders the bound URL sandboxed, reload re-sets the frame src, the viewport switch resizes the frame, and the sandbox + external-URL policy match iframe-embed. The UI dashboard suite (100 tests) is green.

## Scope
Phase 1 only — embed + reload + viewport. Phase 2 (agent-driven dev-server lifecycle + hot-reload) and phase 3 (browser-backed console/network/screenshot so the agent sees its own preview) are follow-on PRs tracked on #101138.

## How it works
The preview widget reuses `resolveEmbedSandbox` and the external-URL gating from `iframe-embed` verbatim — it does **not** weaken the sandbox. The URL comes from the same `static`/`rpc` binding path every builtin uses. The added chrome (reload, viewport) is pure view state around the existing sandboxed frame.

Note: **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged. The diff includes regenerated i18n locale bundles for the new `dashboard.widget.preview.*` keys (via the repo's `ui:i18n:sync` locale workflow); those generated files can be skipped in review.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard has no preview/browser panel (#27574); there's no first-class way to watch a running dev server or a deployed URL inside a workspace. This adds a trusted `builtin:preview` widget with reload + viewport controls, reusing the existing sandboxed embed frame.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 100 passed (the preview widget renders the bound URL in a sandboxed frame, the reload control re-sets `src`, viewport buttons swap the frame width, and the sandbox + external-URL policy match `iframe-embed`); `pnpm ui:build` green; oxlint clean; `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean after regenerating the locale bundles.

target.title: fix: inject completion acknowledgment when tool-only turns produce no text
target.body:
## Summary

When a model turn consists entirely of tool calls (file edits, memory writes, exec commands) with zero visible text in the response, the user sees nothing delivered to Telegram. The operations complete successfully but no message appears in the chat.

## Root Cause

In `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`, when `payloadArray.length === 0`, the code returns `undefined` unconditionally — even when tool calls were successfully executed. This makes the turn invisible to the user.

## Fix

Added a check for `runResult.meta?.toolSummary?.calls > 0` before returning. When tools ran but produced no text payload, a short `"Done."` acknowledgment is injected so the user knows the work completed.

## Testing

- The change is a 6-line addition in a single location
- The fix follows the existing code pattern (`returnWithQueuedFollowupDrain({ text: "..." })`)
- No behavior change when no tools ran (still returns `undefined` as before)
- No behavior change when payloads were produced (skips the empty check entirely)

Closes #79472

target.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — persist widget state via a setState bridge capability
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** approve a stateful custom widget (e.g. the `notes` starter), type, and reload → state persists via the jailed `setState`; a stale `expectedVersion` write is rejected.

---

> Give sandboxed widgets memory: a jailed, approval-gated `setState` capability that turns custom widgets from views into stateful apps.

Closes #101137. **Stacked on #101098** (the sandboxed custom-widget host) — that PR lands first; this targets `main` with a cumulative diff, so review the new `state`-related files as the delta.

## What problem this solves
Custom widgets today are read-only: the postMessage bridge lets a widget *ask* the parent for data, but there's no way to *save* anything — so an agent-built notes pad, kanban, or game resets on every reload. This adds the one missing primitive: per-widget, jailed, size-capped state, without loosening the sandbox.

## What's in this PR
- New gateway RPCs `dashboard.widget.state.get` / `.set` (read/write scoped), persisting to a path-jailed, size-capped per-widget file under `<stateDir>/dashboard/state/<widgetId>.json` — atomic writes, kept *separate* from `workspace.json` (does not count against the 256 KB workspace cap).
- New bridge inbound messages `dashboard:setState` / `getState`, gated behind a new `state:persist` manifest capability (mirrors the existing `sendPrompt` gate).
- The trusted parent resolves the widget's own `widgetId` — a widget can never read or write another widget's state, and a widget-supplied id is ignored.
- Unit tests covering the store round-trip (persist → read-back), the 64 KB size-cap whole-reject, widget-id charset/traversal rejects, the capability gate, read/write scope, and state-vs-workspace separation — the `extensions/dashboard` suite (85 tests) and the UI dashboard suite (94 tests) are green.
- This PR is the capability + its plumbing; the first shippable consumer is the stateful notes/todo widget (#101146), which depends on it.

## How it works
The design mirrors the read path from #101098: **the widget never holds a credential and never talks to the gateway** — the trusted Control-UI parent brokers everything. On `dashboard:setState`, the parent calls `dashboard.widget.state.set` with the `widgetId` *it* already tracks for that iframe (`widget.id`); the widget's message carries only the opaque blob, and the `setWidgetState` bridge dependency takes *only* the blob — there is no code path by which a widget names another widget's state. State is capped at **64 KB** per widget (the serialized envelope, rejected whole *before* any write), stored under `<stateDir>/dashboard/state/<widgetId>.json` (`0o700` dir / `0o600` file), serialized through the store's process mutex and written atomically via `replaceFileAtomic`. The widget id is charset-guarded (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$`) and the resolved path is re-checked for containment. The new `plugin.dashboard.widget-state.changed` broadcast carries `{ widgetId, version }` only — never the blob.

## Security
This widens the trust surface, so it carries the same adversarial-review discipline as #101098. Verified in code and tests:
- **(a) Own-state only** — the `widgetId` is always `widget.id`, bound by the trusted parent; the `setWidgetState` bridge dependency takes only the blob, and any id in the child's message is ignored.
- **(b) Size cap** — 64 KB enforced on the serialized envelope *before* any write; oversize is rejected whole (nothing written).
- **(c) Path jail** — the id is charset-guarded (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,48}$`) and the resolved `state/<widgetId>.json` path is re-checked for containment.
- **(d) Capability gate** — `state:persist` is required; an ungated widget is denied *without touching the gateway*, the same shape as `sendPrompt`.
- **(e) No new iframe reach** — the iframe still cannot reach the gateway; the parent holds the socket and calls the new RPCs on the widget's behalf.
- **(f) Sandbox unchanged** — opaque origin, CSP `connect-src 'none'`, and the window-identity accept filter are all untouched.

Note: this PR adds **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged, so the dependency-graph guard should not trip.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Sandboxed custom widgets cannot persist their own state (the bridge is read-only), so any agent- or user-built interactive widget resets on reload. This adds a jailed, size-capped, capability-gated `setState`/`getState` path so a widget can save and restore its own state.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 85 passed (store persist/read-back round-trip, 64 KB whole-reject, widget-id charset/traversal rejects, capability gate, read/write scope, and proof that widget state is written under `state/<widgetId>.json` and never into `workspace.json`); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 94 passed (bridge routes `setState`/`getState` only when the `state:persist` capability is present, and ignores any widget-supplied id); `pnpm ui:build` and oxlint clean.

target.title: feat(dashboard): sandboxed custom widgets + approval flow [3/3]
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try it:** this branch is the complete substrate — `gh pr checkout 101098 && pnpm install && pnpm build`, start the gateway with the dashboard plugin, open Control UI → **Workspaces**. Scaffold a custom widget and approve the pending card → the sandboxed iframe mounts (pending/rejected assets 404 server-side).

---

# Sandboxed custom widgets + approval flow (3/3)

> **The dashboard your agent builds with you.** This is the capability nothing else in the ecosystem has: an agent authors a real HTML widget, it renders live inside the operator's dashboard, and it does so inside a sandbox strict enough that independent security review couldn't break out of it. This is the last mile between "the agent describes a dashboard" and "the agent builds it."

![End-to-end: an agent scaffolds a custom revenue-chart widget, a pending-approval card appears, the operator approves it, the sandboxed iframe mounts and renders live data through the bridge, then the human keeps working the composed grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/dashboard-demo.gif)

*▶ Full-quality recording ([light](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/modular-dashboard-demo-v1/dashboard-demo.mp4) / [dark](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/modular-dashboard-demo-v1/dashboard-demo-dark.mp4)).*

> **Stack note.** This is the top of a three-PR stack (#101094 backend → #101097 UI → #101098 here). The reviewable new work in *this* PR is the sandboxed custom-widget host — ~1,400 lines of source across 9 files, well under VISION.md's ~5K reviewable-line guideline. Because we don't have upstream write access to set GitHub-native stacked bases, all three PRs target `main` with cumulative diffs, so this branch's diff includes #101094's and #101097's commits until they merge to `main` — **review #101094 and #101097 first, then read this PR's `extensions/dashboard/src/{http-route,serve,manifest}.ts` and `ui/src/{components/dashboard-custom-widget,lib/dashboard/bridge}.ts` as the delta.** This same branch is also the full feature end-to-end — check it out to run everything.

## Run the whole thing

Because this PR sits at the top of the stack, checking it out gives you the complete modular-dashboard feature in one branch — no need to assemble the stack yourself:

```sh
gh pr checkout <this-PR-number>       # or: git fetch <fork> feat/modular-dashboard && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
pnpm install && pnpm build
# start the gateway with the dashboard plugin enabled, open the Control UI → the "Workspaces" tab
```

The default **Overview-as-data** workspace renders on first load. Ask an agent (or run `openclaw dashboard tabs create --title Financials`) to build a tab and watch it appear live; scaffold a custom widget, approve it from the pending card, and watch the sandboxed iframe mount. CI runs against this full integration.

## What problem this solves

#101094 and #101097 get an operator most of the way there with a live grid and trusted, built-in widgets — but the actual bet of this whole series is that an agent can build something *bespoke*: a chart, a custom view, a one-off tool, authored on the spot in response to "build me a revenue chart." That means running agent-authored code inside the operator's browser, which is the one place in this series that needs to be provably safe before it ships, not just believed safe.

## What's in this PR

- **Scaffold → pending → approve → mount lifecycle.** An agent (via the `dashboard_widget_scaffold` tool from #101094) creates a widget directory with a manifest and an `index.html`; it enters the registry as `status: "pending"`. A pending widget renders as a placeholder card (name, author, Approve/Reject) — **no iframe is ever created for a pending or rejected widget, on either the client or the server.** Approval routes through the existing plugin-approvals infrastructure as well as an inline Approve button, so it shows up wherever operators already look for approvals.
- **Sandboxed iframe host** (`ui/src/components/dashboard-custom-widget.ts`): `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` — never `allow-same-origin`, never any other token. The sandbox attribute is treated as a constant, not configuration.
- **A versioned, minimal postMessage bridge** (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bridge.ts`): the widget can ask for its declared data bindings and a theme snapshot, and — only with an explicit manifest capability plus a per-invocation operator confirm dialog — ask to send a prompt into chat. The parent only ever accepts messages from the exact iframe window it created, only recognizes a fixed set of message types, and only resolves bindings the widget's own manifest declared — a widget cannot request data it wasn't given permission to see.
- **Static-file-only asset serving**: a new unauthenticated plugin HTTP route (necessary — sandboxed frames carry no device token) that serves *only* files inside the widget's own directory, behind a charset check on the widget name, path normalization, and a containment check, with a locked-down `Content-Security-Policy` (including `connect-src 'none'`, so "no network" is structural, not just a convention) on every response. Only `approved` widgets are served at all — pending/rejected widgets 404 server-side, independent of whatever the client does.
- **Theme sync**: widgets receive the Control UI's current theme tokens so agent-authored UI matches the operator's chosen theme (including #99289's light palette) without the widget author having to guess.

## See it

The full scaffold → pending → approve → mount → live lifecycle, one frame at a time:

**1. Pending — the iframe does not exist yet.** A scaffolded widget lands as a placeholder card (name, author, Approve/Reject). No iframe is constructed on the client, and the assets 404 server-side, until an operator approves.

![A custom widget in the pending-approval card: "Revenue Chart — awaiting approval, built by finance agent," with Approve and Reject affordances and no iframe rendered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/03-financials-pending-approval.png)

**2. Approved and mounted.** After the operator approves, the sandboxed iframe mounts and renders — here an approved custom chart widget on the composed Financials tab, alongside AI-provenance chips and the finance-activity lifecycle feed.

![The composed Financials tab with the approved, sandboxed custom widget rendering a chart, AI-provenance chips, and the Finance Activity lifecycle feed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/04-approved-sandboxed-chart.png)

**3. Live.** A bound value updates in place as the finance agent writes new data — the widget never fetched anything; the parent pushed the resolved binding over the bridge.

![The approved custom widget with a bound revenue value updating live, driven by a data push through the bridge rather than any network call from the widget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/05-live-revenue-update.png)

The same composed Financials tab in the dark theme, kebab menu open, sandboxed widget rendering — agent-authored UI adopts the operator's theme tokens automatically:

![Dark theme: the composed Financials dashboard with the sandboxed custom widget rendering and a widget cell's kebab menu open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/financials-composed-dark.png)

## How it works

The design principle is one sentence: **the widget is untrusted agent-authored code, so it gets no origin, no network, no credentials, and no direct line to the gateway — the trusted parent does everything on its behalf.** Every mechanism below is a consequence of that.

### The key insight: the widget never talks to the gateway

A custom widget is HTML/JS an *agent* wrote. It renders in the operator's browser but is treated as hostile. It has no way to reach the gateway: the sandbox denies it an origin, the CSP denies it the network, and it holds no token. All data reaches it through a single narrow channel — the parent resolves the widget's *declared* bindings and posts the results in. If the widget wants data it wasn't granted, there is no request it can make that succeeds. That inversion (parent-resolves-on-behalf, never widget-fetches) is what makes running agent-authored code in the operator's browser defensible.

### Rendering — a constant `allow-scripts` sandbox

The host component (`ui/src/components/dashboard-custom-widget.ts`) mounts `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" referrerpolicy="no-referrer">`. The sandbox attribute is a **constant string**, not configuration — never `allow-same-origin`, never `allow-top-navigation`, `allow-popups`, or `allow-forms`. With `allow-scripts` alone, the frame's origin is opaque (serializes as `"null"`), so it can never touch the parent's storage, cookies, or DOM. The code comments call this out explicitly ("do not templatize") so a future well-meaning edit can't loosen it.

### Serving — a static-only, path-jailed, approval-gated route

Sandboxed frames carry no device token, so the asset route (`extensions/dashboard/src/http-route.ts`) is registered `auth:"plugin"` (unauthenticated). That is safe *only because* the route is static-file-only and can leak nothing:

- **Name and path**: `/plugins/dashboard/widgets/<name>/<path...>` — `<name>` passes the canvas charset check (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`); `<path...>` is URL-decoded, logically normalized, and containment-checked against the widget's own directory (the `extensions/canvas/src/documents.ts` idiom, reused verbatim).
- **Every rejection is a 404, never a 403** — a traversal attempt, a bad charset, a disallowed extension, or a non-GET method is indistinguishable from a miss, so the route leaks no existence information.
- **Content type is allowlisted by extension** (html/js/css/json/svg/png/jpg/webp/woff2/txt/md/csv); anything else 404s.
- **Strict CSP on every response**: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. `connect-src 'none'` makes "no network" **structural**, not conventional.
- **Approval gate at serve time**: the handler checks the registry and serves *only* widgets whose `status === "approved"`. Pending/rejected widgets 404 server-side, independent of anything the client does — so approval-bypass is enforced where the bytes are, not merely in the UI.

### The bridge — versioned, window-identity-filtered, allowlist-re-checked

Data reaches the widget through a versioned postMessage bridge (`ui/src/lib/dashboard/bridge.ts`, envelope `{ v:1, type, … }`), whose security logic is deliberately DOM-free so it's unit-testable in isolation:

- **Accept filter by window identity**: the parent accepts a message only when `event.source === iframe.contentWindow`. Origin strings are useless here (a sandboxed origin is `"null"`), so identity is the check — a message from any other window, including a second widget's iframe, is dropped.
- **Fixed message set, declared bindings only**: the parent recognizes a closed set of types and resolves only bindings the widget's *own manifest* declared, by `bindingId`. `file`/`static` bindings resolve via `dashboard.data.read` (server re-validates the jail); `rpc` bindings are called by the parent on its own gateway client — and the method is **re-checked at resolve time** against the browser-side mirror of the plugin's write-time allowlist (`RPC_METHOD_ALLOWLIST`), a defense-in-depth check on top of PR1's write-time gate. A widget cannot request a binding or method it wasn't granted.
- **Parent→child posts use `targetOrigin "*"`** (required for an opaque child origin) — acceptable *by construction* because the only payloads ever posted are binding data and theme tokens the widget is already entitled to. No config, no session data, no tokenized URLs are ever sent.
- **`sendPrompt` is triple-gated**: it requires the manifest capability `prompt:send`, then a per-invocation operator **confirm dialog** quoting the exact text, then it's **rate-limited** (1 in-flight + 10/min per widget) before it reaches the existing chat-send path.
- **Theme sync**: `getTheme` returns the Control UI's current CSS custom-property tokens (including #99289's light palette) so agent-authored UI matches the operator's theme without the author guessing.

### Approval lifecycle

An agent-scaffolded widget (`dashboard_widget_scaffold`, from #101094) enters `widgetsRegistry` as `status:"pending"`. A pending widget renders the placeholder card — **no iframe is constructed, client or server**. Approval routes through the existing plugin-approvals infrastructure (so it appears wherever operators already look for approvals) as well as the card's inline Approve button → `dashboard.widget.approve` → re-broadcast. Only `approved` widgets ever get an iframe, and only `approved` widgets are ever served — the gate is double-enforced, UI and server.

### Then we tried to break it

This layer got an independent adversarial security review before being proposed here, specifically because it's the highest-security-surface part of the project. The review's job was to try to refute three claims — the path-jail on asset serving, the iframe sandbox, and the CSP — and it could not refute any of them, across two independent passes and dozens of live probes against the running implementation (path traversal variants, encoded/absolute/backslash/symlink-out paths, sandbox-attribute inspection, and a live `connect-src 'none'` network test).

The review did find one real gap: a prompt-dispatch rate limit that didn't survive a widget being removed and re-added (a remount could reset the counter). That was fixed — the rate limiter is now keyed independently of widget lifecycle and covered by a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after — plus a second, defense-in-depth check added at resolve time and a test that keeps the UI-side allowlist mirror in sync with the server-side one. Nothing else from the review was left open.

The resulting safety story, concretely:
- **Rendering** is `allow-scripts` only — no `allow-same-origin`, so the iframe's origin is opaque and it can never touch the parent's storage, cookies, or DOM.
- **Serving** is static-file-only, path-jailed, and gated on registry approval status server-side — approval bypass isn't a client-trust question, it's enforced where the bytes are served from.
- **Networking** is structurally blocked (`connect-src 'none'` in the CSP), not just discouraged by convention.
- **Data** only ever reaches the widget through the bridge, resolved by the authenticated parent against the widget's own declared bindings — the widget itself never holds a credential and never talks to the gateway directly.
- **Prompt dispatch** is capability-gated in the manifest, confirm-dialog-gated per invocation, and rate-limited independent of the widget's mount/unmount lifecycle.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Agents cannot author bespoke widgets that render in the operator's dashboard, because running agent-authored HTML in the browser is unsafe without a hard sandbox. This PR adds the sandboxed custom-widget host: an `allow-scripts`-only iframe (opaque origin), a static-only, path-jailed, approval-gated serving route with `connect-src 'none'`, and a window-identity-filtered postMessage bridge where the trusted parent resolves the widget's declared bindings on its behalf — so an agent-scaffolded widget renders only after operator approval and never talks to the gateway directly.

**Evidence:** 79 plugin + 284 UI tests pass, including the path-jail suite (traversal, encoded traversal, absolute, backslash, symlink-out, name-charset, disallowed extension, non-GET → all 404 with `Content-Security-Policy` + `X-Content-Type-Options` asserted on every response), the bridge suite (foreign-window postMessage dropped, undeclared-binding denial, `sendPrompt` capability-gate + confirm dialog + rate limit), and the custom-widget E2E (approve → mount, a live `fetch()` from the widget blocked by CSP, the sandbox attribute asserted to be exactly `allow-scripts`, and the kill test). An independent adversarial review could not refute the path-jail, sandbox, or CSP across two passes and dozens of live probes; the one hole it found (a prompt rate limit that reset on widget remount) is fixed with a regression test that fails before and passes after. The scaffold → pending → approve → mount → live lifecycle is in the stills above and the recording.

## Verification

**Size:** ~1,400 lines of reviewable source across 9 files (the sandboxed-widget host) — comfortably inside VISION.md's ~5K reviewable-line guideline.

- Path-jail suite: traversal (`../`), encoded traversal, absolute paths, backslash variants, symlink-out, name-charset violations, disallowed extensions, non-GET requests — all 404, with correct `Content-Security-Policy` and `X-Content-Type-Options` headers asserted on every response.
- Bridge suite: handshake, foreign-window postMessage correctly ignored, unknown message types dropped, undeclared binding requests denied, `sendPrompt` without capability denied without even showing a dialog, with capability shows the dialog and sends exactly once on confirm / nothing on deny, rate-limit behavior under remount.
- E2E: `connect-src 'none'` asserted against a live `fetch()` from inside a widget; sandbox attribute asserted to be exactly `allow-scripts` via DOM inspection; the kill test (a throwing widget produces an isolated error card, siblings and other tabs unaffected); the full approve → mount → live-update round trip against a fixture widget.
- The plugin serve/manifest/path-jail suites and the UI bridge + custom-widget suites pass (79 plugin + 284 UI tests), plus the custom-widget E2E (approve → mount, foreign-window drop, CSP `fetch()` block, sandbox-attribute assertion, kill test). CI runs on this PR.

## Closes / part of

Closes **#66983** / **#68497** (agent-rendered UI reachable from the browser — this is exactly that, with the safety work done up front). Partially addresses **#27574** (browser preview panel — the custom-widget host covers the "agent shows me something in the browser" half; a dedicated standalone preview panel outside the dashboard grid is not in scope here). Part of #101093. Builds on #101094, #101097 (top of the stack). With all three merged, the full end-to-end flow in the recording above — agent composes a tab, scaffolds and approves a sandboxed widget, live updates, human reorders — is reproducible against a running gateway.
