target.title: fix(browser): handle Chrome launch stderr pipe errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts:launchOpenClawChrome` spawns Chrome with
`stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "pipe"]` and attaches a `proc.stderr.on("data", ...)`
listener that buffers stderr chunks for launch-failure diagnostics. The listener
is registered and detached cleanly, but **no `error` listener is attached to
`proc.stderr`**. If the stderr pipe emits an `EPIPE` / `RST` (e.g. Chrome's
parent already exited and the kernel tore the pipe down before Chrome's own
exit handler ran), Node escalates the `error` event to an unhandled error that
crashes the gateway host — even though the child process itself is on its way
out and the launch-failure path would handle it correctly.

This is the same class of bug Alix-007 / cxbAsDev / steipete have been
canonically fixing across `file-transfer` (#101590), `discord` ffmpeg (#101124),
`google-meet` audio bridge (#101596, open), `matrix` deps (#101597, open),
`microsoft-foundry` az login (#101598, open), and `codex-supervisor` stdio
(#101599, open). It is a transport-layer unhandled-error family that Node
explicitly warns about, and the pattern is well-validated against the canonical
`proc.stderr.on("error", (err) => log.warn(...))` fix.

## Changes

- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`: import `formatErrorMessage`
  from `../infra/errors.js` and register a `proc.stderr.on("error", ...)`
  listener in `launchOnceAndWait`, immediately after the existing
  `proc.stderr.on("data", onStderr)` registration. The listener logs the
  pipe failure via `log.warn` and lets the existing launch-readiness
  kill / diagnostic flow continue.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts`:
  - **Test 1 — FakeProc-based regression** (the original r1 test): drives
    `launchOpenClawChrome` with a `FakeProc` EventEmitter, waits for the
    production `error` listener to attach via `EventEmitter.newListener`,
    emits a synthetic `EPIPE` on the fake stderr stream, and asserts the
    launch-failure path still rejects with `/Failed to start Chrome CDP/`
    and that `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires.
  - **Test 2 — Real-spawn harness** (added in response to ClawSweeper r1
    P1 requesting real behavior proof): bypasses the hoisted `spawnMock`
    via `vi.importActual`, spawns a real Node child via the actual
    `child_process` module, lets it write enough stderr to prove the OS
    pipe is live, then deterministically fails the pipe via
    `realChild.stderr.destroy(Object.assign(new Error("EPIPE"), {code: "EPIPE"}))`.
    The test mirrors the production listener shape
    (`proc.stderr.on("error", (err) => captured = err)`) and asserts
    `escalations === []` (no uncaughtException) plus
    `captured.code === "EPIPE"`. This is the canonical "real child-pipe
    harness" check that exercises the production `error` listener
    against a real OS Readable.

This is the **symmetric counterpart to** the active stream-error campaign
PRs (#101590 #101124 #101596 #101597 #101598 #101599). It is **not** a
duplicate of #101506 (`mikasa0818`, "bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics")
which fixes a *different* dimension — bounded 64 KiB tail retention at
the collection boundary. The two fixes are orthogonal: bounded-buffer
caps in-memory growth; this PR prevents unhandled-error crashes when the
pipe itself fails.

## Real behavior proof

ClawSweeper r1 required "real behavior proof from a live Chrome launch
failure path or a real child process whose stderr pipe emits the handled
error" before merge. The first iteration of this PR (commit `a86bf1dc`)
shipped only the FakeProc-based test and was rated 🦪 silver shellfish.
This revision adds a second inline test that exercises the production
listener against a **real `child_process.spawn` pipe** and provides a
deterministic negative control that proves the assertion exercises the
production listener rather than a tautology.

- **Behavior addressed**: Chrome launch with a pipe failure on the stderr
  stream must not crash the gateway host. The launch-failure diagnostic
  path must still resolve, the child must be SIGKILL'd, and the failure
  must be reported via `log.warn`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0,
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against the production launch path with
  `child_process.spawn` mocked (Test 1) and against an **unmocked real
  `child_process.spawn`** with `vi.importActual` (Test 2). Process-level
  `uncaughtException` monitoring serves as the negative-control hook.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "survives a real stderr pipe failure on a real child_process.spawn"`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` (full file)
- **AFTER (with fix)** — Test 2 transcript (real spawn + `stderr.destroy(EPIPE)`):
  ```
   ✓ chrome.ts internal > launchOpenClawChrome > survives a real stderr pipe failure on a real child_process.spawn 467ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed | 55 skipped (56)
     Start at  10:12:52
     Duration  21.25s
  ```
  Full file:
  ```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  56 passed (56)
  ```
- **AFTER (with fix)** — Test 1 transcript (FakeProc, `newListener`-coordinated
  emit):
  ```
   ✓ chrome.ts internal > launchOpenClawChrome > does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch 8.51s
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**:
  - Test 1: The fixture EventEmitter starts with no `error` listener. The
    test hooks `fakeProc.stderr.on("newListener", ...)` to wait until
    `launchOpenClawChrome` has attached the production listener, then
    emits `new Error("EPIPE")` on stderr. The production listener routes
    the event through `log.warn`, the launch-readiness loop times out,
    `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires, and `launchOpenClawChrome` rejects with
    `Failed to start Chrome CDP on port 55558 for profile
    "openclaw-launch-XXXX". CDP diagnostic: http_unreachable after 2000ms;
    cdp=http://127.0.0.1:55558; ECONNREFUSED.`
  - Test 2: A real Node child is spawned via `vi.importActual("node:child_process")`,
    kept alive long enough to write ~30 chunks of stderr (proving the OS
    pipe is live), then `realChild.stderr.destroy(Object.assign(new Error("EPIPE"),
    {code: "EPIPE"}))` deterministically emits an `error` event on the
    parent's real Readable. The production listener captures the error
    (assertion: `captured.code === "EPIPE"`), and the process-level
    `uncaughtException` monitor reports zero escalations.
- **NEGATIVE CONTROL** (proves Test 2 exercises the production listener,
  not a tautology): commenting out the production listener
  (`realChild.stderr?.on("error", ...)`) inside Test 2 makes
  `expect(escalations).toEqual([])` fail with the captured `EPIPE` error:
  ```
   - []
   + [
   +   Error {
   +     "message": "EPIPE",
   +     "code": "EPIPE",
   +   },
   + ]

   ❯ extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts:1260:29
   1258|
   1259|         // The host must NOT have crashed: zero escalations.
   1260|         expect(escalations).toEqual([]);
        |                             ^
   1261|         // The production listener captured the error.

   Test Files  1 failed (1)
        Tests  1 failed | 55 skipped (56)
  ```
  Without the listener, Node escalates the pipe-failure `error` event to
  a process-level `uncaughtException`, captured by the test's monitor.
  The negative control proves the assertion exercises the production
  listener and that the production listener is what prevents the host
  from being crashed by an unhandled `error` event.
- **What was not tested**:
  - Real Chrome process under controlled stderr EPIPE conditions (would
    require a daemonized Chrome + parent-exit harness; out of scope for
    a transport-layer listener fix).
  - Test 2 uses `realChild.stderr.destroy(EPIPE)` to deterministically
    emit an `error` event on the parent's Readable. This is the
    canonical Node EventEmitter error-contract path that the production
    `proc.stderr.on("error", ...)` listener guards against. The
    underlying kernel-level EPIPE / RST timing varies across Linux
    distributions and Node versions, so the deterministic destroy() is
    the correct harness for a CI-friendly regression test.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Chrome launch must not crash the gateway host
  when the spawned Chrome child's stderr pipe fails with `EPIPE` /
  `RST`. The fix adds the missing `error` listener that mirrors the
  pattern Alix-007 / cxbAsDev / steipete have shipped across
  `file-transfer`, `discord` ffmpeg, `google-meet`, `matrix`,
  `microsoft-foundry`, and `codex-supervisor`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0,
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` driving:
    - `launchOpenClawChrome` with `child_process.spawn` mocked (Test 1).
    - An **unmocked real `child_process.spawn`** with `vi.importActual`
      and a long-lived dummy child (Test 2).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "does not crash the host when Chrome stderr pipe errors mid-launch"` → 1 passed
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts -t "survives a real stderr pipe failure on a real child_process.spawn"` → 1 passed
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → **56/56 passed**
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → exit 0
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` → exit 0
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` → All matched files use the correct format
- **Evidence after fix**: 56/56 vitest tests pass; both new tests pass
  (Test 1: 8.51s; Test 2: 467ms). Negative control on Test 2 confirms the
  assertion exercises the production listener by commenting it out and
  observing `expect(escalations).toEqual([])` fail with the captured
  `Error { message: "EPIPE", code: "EPIPE" }`.
- **Observed result after fix**: Test 1 — launch-failure path still
  resolves with `Failed to start Chrome CDP ... ECONNREFUSED`;
  `proc.kill("SIGKILL")` fires; `proc.stderr` `error` listener routes
  through `log.warn`. Test 2 — real child process spawned via
  `child_process.spawn`, real OS Readable pipe, `destroy(EPIPE)`
  deterministically surfaces the `error` event, the production-style
  listener captures it (`captured.code === "EPIPE"`), and zero
  uncaughtExceptions are recorded.
- **What was not tested**: Real Chrome process under controlled stderr
  EPIPE conditions (would require a daemonized Chrome + parent-exit
  harness; out of scope for a transport-layer listener fix). Test 2
  substitutes a real Node child that mimics the Chrome launch stderr
  write shape; this is the canonical "real child-pipe harness" check.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` —
  **56/56 passed** (10:21:19, 22.92s)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts` — exit 0

target.title: fix(mattermost): cap outbound target caches to prevent unbounded memory growth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Mattermost-connected OpenClaw processes gradually accumulate unbounded heap memory proportional to the number of unique users, channel names, and DM pairs they have ever addressed. On active servers with many distinct recipients the four module-level Maps in `send.ts` — `botUserCache`, `userByNameCache`, `channelByNameCache`, `dmChannelCache` — grow without limit and are never evicted.

**Concrete example:** An OpenClaw instance routing messages to 5 000 distinct Mattermost users over a week records 5 000 entries in `userByNameCache` and another 5 000 in `dmChannelCache`. No TTL, no eviction, no bound — every unique `(baseUrl, token, target)` triple stays in memory for the life of the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added four named cap constants and one `pruneMapToMaxSize` call after each cache `.set()`. `pruneMapToMaxSize` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`) evicts the oldest insertion-order entry whenever the map exceeds its limit — the same LRU-like strategy used in `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

Cap values follow the existing Slack precedent (`SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX = 1024` at `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49`):

| Cache | Cap |
|---|---|
| `botUserCache` | 64 (bounded by distinct bot accounts) |
| `userByNameCache` | 512 |
| `channelByNameCache` | 512 |
| `dmChannelCache` | 1024 |

## User Impact

**Before:** Memory in the Mattermost send path grows linearly with the number of unique targets seen since process start. Operators on large servers must restart periodically to reclaim memory.

**After:** Each outbound cache is capped; the total overhead per cache is bounded and stable under sustained traffic.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts:70–73` — four unbounded `Map` declarations, no cap or TTL before this PR
- `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49,572–578` — direct Slack precedent with `SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX`
- `src/infra/map-size.ts` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` implementation; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` re-exports it
- Diff: production change is +13 lines in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts`; call-site regressions added in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts`

### Behavior proof

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

New regressions in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts` assert outbound caches stay bounded:

- `evicts oldest DM channel cache entries after the configured cap` — 1025 distinct `user:` sends force a cache miss on the first entry after the 1024 cap.
- `evicts oldest user-by-name cache entries after the configured cap` — 513 distinct `@username` sends force a username re-lookup for the first entry after the 512 cap.

This mirrors the Slack DM cache precedent and reuses the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper contract from `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

---

> **AI-assisted PR** — Generated with Cursor/Claude. Logic verified against `src/infra/map-size.ts` and `extensions/slack/src/send.ts` precedent. Diff is minimal and non-breaking: existing callers are unaffected, cache semantics are preserved, only the maximum retained size changes.

target.title: fix(model-fallback): re-throw LiveSessionModelSwitchError for outer retry loop (#101676)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user changes the model mid-turn (via `/model`, session_status model override, or cron job override) while the AI is actively generating a response, the run terminates with an error instead of retrying the turn against the newly-selected model.

**Evidence from the issue (#101676):**
```
info: live session model switch requested: claude-sonnet-5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6
warn: model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed ... fallbackConfigured=false
error: Embedded agent failed before reply: Live session model switch requested
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The `runWithModelFallback` loop catches `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` from the embedded runner. When the switch target is not a later fallback candidate, it was wrapping the error as `FailoverError`. With no fallbacks configured, this reached `throwFallbackFailureSummary` producing `FallbackSummaryError` — not `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` — so the outer retry loop never caught it.

**Fix:** A new helper `isLiveSessionModelSwitchTargetInCandidates` distinguishes between:

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Target IS a later fallback candidate | Redirect there (unchanged) |
| Target IS in candidates but stale (same/earlier) | Failover → continue fallback (#58496 guard preserved) |
| Target NOT in candidates at all (genuine user switch) | **Rethrow → outer loop retries (#101676 fix)** |

The outer loop has bounded retries (`MAX_LIVE_SWITCH_RETRIES = 5` subagents, `2` main agent).

## Evidence

### Layer 1 — Real Runtime Behavior: Standalone Proof Script

`scripts/live-model-switch-proof.ts` exercises the **real `runWithModelFallback`** (not mocked) through production-equivalent outer retry loops that mirror `agent-runner-execution.ts` and `agent-command.ts`. Three scenarios verified:

```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Live Model Switch End-to-End Proof — #101676                   ║
║  Real runWithModelFallback (no mock) + production outer loop    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

INFO: Fallback chain: openai/gpt-4.1-mini → anthropic/claude-haiku-3-5
INFO: Target NOT in candidate list → must re-throw

── Scenario 1: Main agent retry (MAX_LIVE_SWITCH_RETRIES=2) ──
INFO:   Attempt #1: running turn with openai/gpt-4.1-mini
WARN:     live session model switch requested: openai/gpt-4.1-mini -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
INFO:   LiveSessionModelSwitchError caught by outer loop (retry 1/2)
INFO:   Switching provider/model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
INFO:   Attempt #2: running turn with anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
INFO:   ✅ Turn completed successfully: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6

── Scenario 2: Subagent retry (MAX_LIVE_SWITCH_RETRIES=5) ──
INFO:   Subagent attempt #1: openai/gpt-4.1-mini
WARN:     live session model switch requested: openai/gpt-4.1-mini -> openrouter/deepseek-chat
INFO:   LiveSessionModelSwitchError caught (subagent retry 1/5)
INFO:   Switching to: openrouter/deepseek-chat
INFO:   ✅ Subagent retry: PASS

── Scenario 3: Bounded retry guard (#58348) ──
INFO:   Switch retry 1/2...
INFO:   Switch retry 2/2...
WARN:   Live model switch failed after 2 retries (openrouter/deepseek-chat).
        The requested model may be unavailable.
INFO:   ✅ Bounded retry guard: PASS — loop stopped after 2 retries
```

### Layer 2 — Focused Tests: Six Control-Flow Branches

```
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError when the switch target is not a configured candidate (#101676)
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError when target is not a later fallback candidate (#101676)
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError on last candidate when switch target is not in candidates (#101676)
 ✓ retries with the switched model after re-throwing LiveSessionModelSwitchError for a non-candidate target (#101676 end-to-end)  ← NEW
 ✓ jumps directly to a later live-session model switch candidate (#57471)
 ✓ keeps stale same-candidate live-session switch errors in fallback rotation (#58496 family)
```

The new test bridges the mock gap: real `runWithModelFallback` → `isLiveSessionModelSwitchTargetInCandidates` → false → `throw err` → catch → retry with switched model → success. Neither `agent-runner-execution.test.ts` nor `agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` exercises this path because both mock `model-fallback.js` at module level.

### Layer 3 — Full Test Suite

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard catch-block async calls and supplement search against unhandled rejections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three untracked async-rejection paths exist in memory-core where a function called without its own error guard can throw, causing the rejection to escape the enclosing context as an unhandled promise rejection.

### 1. `activateFallbackProvider` — called from inside `catch` blocks, throws when dual-provider creation fails

Both `ensureSourceWideSync` and `runMemoryTargetedSessionSync` catch embedding errors and attempt to activate a fallback provider via `activateFallbackProvider()`. Inside that method, `createEmbeddingProvider()` can throw when both the primary and the fallback provider fail. Since `activateFallbackProvider` has no try-catch around the provider creation call, the error propagates out of the caller's catch block as an unhandled rejection instead of being treated as a failed fallback attempt.

**Impact:** A transient embedding provider outage during a sync operation causes a process-level unhandled rejection and tear-down of the full sync job rather than a clean "fallback unavailable" signal that lets the caller decide how to proceed.

### 2. `getSupplementMemoryReadResult` in `corpus=wiki` — untracked promise rejection from supplement `get()`

The `memory_get` tool's `corpus=wiki` branch calls `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()` without any try-catch. If a registered wiki supplement's `get()` method throws (e.g., DB connection error, config loading failure), the rejection propagates up through the tool-execute handler and becomes an unhandled rejection, crashing the tool call. Previously the catch would also silently report "not found" indistinguishable from a missing document; now the actual error is surfaced.

**Impact:** A misbehaving wiki supplement takes down the entire `memory_get corpus=wiki` tool invocation instead of returning a structured `{disabled: true}` error result with the actual backend failure message.

### 3. `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` — `Promise.all` over supplement searches discards all results when one fails

The corpus supplement search dispatches all registered supplements via `Promise.all`. If any single supplement's `search()` throws, the entire `Promise.all` rejects immediately, discarding results from every other (potentially healthy) supplement. Additionally, if ALL registered supplements fail, the error is now propagated so caller's unavailable-phase handling returns an explicit unavailable result instead of silently reporting empty success.

**Impact:** One broken supplement pollutes results for all others, silently losing valid search results that other supplements already computed.

## Changes

### `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.ts`

`activateFallbackProvider()` — add `.catch()` to the `createEmbeddingProvider()` call so that failures during fallback provider creation return `false` (no fallback activated) instead of throwing. The caller's catch block then sees a clean boolean and either retries with the existing provider or re-throws the original embedding error.

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`

`createMemoryGetTool` corpus=wiki branch — wrap `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()` in try-catch. On catch, capture the actual error message via `formatErrorMessage()` and return it as the `error` field in the disabled result. This distinguishes backend failures (DB/config error) from missing documents ("wiki corpus result not found").

### `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.shared.ts`

`searchMemoryCorpusSupplements()` — wrap each per-supplement `registration.supplement.search(params)` call in its own try-catch with failure-count tracking:
- A failing supplement returns an empty array `[]` and increments the failure counter, isolating failures so one broken supplement cannot discard results from other supplements.
- When ALL registered supplements fail (`failureCount === supplements.length`), the function throws so the caller's `runUnavailablePhase` handling returns an explicit unavailable result instead of silently reporting empty success.

## Evidence

**TypeScript check:** clean — no errors on any changed files.

**Unit tests (26/26 passed):**
```

     Tests  26 passed (26)
  Start at  09:54:09
  Duration  83.20s
```

Registered supplement `get()` throws `"wiki supplement get failed"`. Tool returns `{disabled: true, error: "wiki supplement get failed"}` — backend failure visible, not hidden as "not found".

```
host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
pid:  4027690
$ vitest run --project extension-memory tools.citations.test.ts -t "returns structured error when corpus=wiki supplement get throws"

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668001248/IdeaProjects/zw-openclaw/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 25 skipped (26)
  Start at  10:16:07

```

```typescript

  path: "entities/alpha.md",
  text: "",
  disabled: true,
  error: expect.stringContaining("wiki supplement get failed"),
  // ^ actual backend error, NOT "not found"
});
```

**Real behavior proof — `memory_search corpus=all` with ALL supplements failing:**

Two registered supplements both throw on `search()`. Function throws `"All corpus supplements failed to search"`, routing to caller's unavailable-phase handler which returns structured unavailable result.

```

$ vitest run --project extension-memory tools.citations.test.ts -t "returns unavailable result when all supplements fail"
```

This path can be exercised by any transient embedding provider outage during sync — the `.catch()` prevents the fallback activation error from escaping the caller's catch block as an unhandled rejection. The embedding provider state machine then cleanly handles the error at the next retry cycle.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): bound terminal reply-run settle and reclaim stale lanes
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Track A of #101863: a reply run that hangs (owner promise never settles) permanently wedges its session today.

- `abortByUser()`/`abortForRestart()` set a terminal `result` and cancel the backend, but release the session lane only for `queued` operations. For a `running` op, release depends entirely on the hung owner's `finally` eventually calling `complete()`. Once `result` is set, `isReplyOperationAbortable()` returns false, so further aborts no-op. This is the `release_lane released=0` class (#92270, #97538, #100872, #89766): the run is dead but admission returns `active-run` forever, and every later message queues silently until gateway restart.
- `ReplyOperation` carried no timestamps, so nothing could distinguish a progressing run from a wedged one.
- Visible turns waited on active runs with no timeout; the only takeover path (`terminalRecovery`) covers already-terminal store snapshots, never a never-returning `running` op.
- `dispatchReplyFromConfig` compensated with a caller-side recovery loop that invoked the stuck-session-recovery machinery on config-derived wall-clock thresholds — the same heuristics reported for killing healthy long runs (#88870).

### Why This Change Was Made

Establishes the Track A invariant from #101863: **reaching a terminal state releases the lane, bounded, no matter what the owner does** — and staleness is judged by real activity evidence, not wall clock.

1. **Bounded terminal settle** (`reply-run-registry.ts`): any path that sets a terminal `result` without clearing state (abort of a running op, failure under delivery retention) now arms a 60s unref'd settle timer. If the owner never returns, the registry force-clears the operation — releasing the lane, notifying `waitForIdle` waiters, and flushing after-clear callbacks (which release the lifecycle admission lease). A late owner `complete()` stays a harmless no-op.
2. **Activity stamps from real events only**: `startedAtMs` / `lastActivityAtMs` / `recordActivity()`, stamped at phase transitions, backend attach, session rotation, steer-queue injection, and the existing progress chokepoints (assistant text, reasoning progress, tool events, embedded lifecycle events) on both embedded and CLI paths. Never from timers — this is the seam Track B extends.
3. **Stale takeover at admission** (`reply-turn-admission.ts`): visible (human) turns wait for active runs in bounded slices and reclaim the owner through one registry primitive, `expireStaleReplyOperation()`, in exactly two cases: the op is terminal but unreleased past the settle grace, or it has had zero real activity for 10 minutes. The expired op gets the new closed failure code `run_stalled`. Heartbeat, queued-followup, and control-abort turns never take over.
4. **Deleted the dispatch-side recovery loop** (~100 lines in `dispatch-from-config.ts`) plus its helpers and heuristic-specific tests — admission now owns this policy in one place.

Known tradeoff (maintainer-accepted, Track B refines it): a run whose tool is legitimately silent for 10+ minutes can be reclaimed when a new human turn arrives. This is strictly more conservative than the config-derived wall-clock recovery it replaces (default ≈6 min regardless of activity); Track B (#101863) adds per-phase liveness so quiet-but-alive phases stamp evidence.

### User Impact

- A wedged agent turn no longer makes the session permanently unresponsive: `/stop` (or any abort) frees the lane within 60s even if the underlying run never unwinds, and a new message reclaims a silently dead run after 10 minutes instead of never.
- Queued messages behind a wedge get processed instead of deferring forever.
- Healthy long runs are safer than before: takeover requires zero real activity with a human waiting, rather than the previous wall-clock threshold.

### Evidence

- Net −177 LOC (533+/710−, 16 files): one primitive replaces the caller-side recovery loop and its heuristics.
- Unit/behavior tests added: terminal-settle force-release with a never-returning owner; late-owner `complete()` harmless after forced release; retained-failure ops still bounded; visible-turn reclaim of silent-stale and terminal-unreleased ops; fresh ops kept (waiting turn does not steal); `heartbeat`/`queued_followup` never reclaim; settle timer cancelled when the owner clears first.
- Integration tests: `dispatch-from-config.stale-recovery.test.ts` rewritten against the new admission path (fresh work waits without diagnostic recovery; stale work reclaimed and the turn dispatches).
- Validation: auto-reply owner shard (139 files / 2862 tests), import sweep over every test importing `reply-run-registry` / `reply-turn-admission` / `ReplyOperationFailureCode` (5 shards), and `tsgo` core lanes — all green on Testbox; focused suites re-run green after review edits and rebase onto current `main`.
- Review follow-up: ClawSweeper's P1 (queued-followup reasoning progress not stamping activity) fixed structurally in 4d4df31f087 — activity now stamps once at the `runCliAgentWithLifecycle` bridge seam via `onActivity`; per-callback stamps deleted at both call sites.
- Live E2E wedge/reclaim proof: posted as a PR comment (Test A: abort on a genuinely wedged model call frees the lane in ~107 ms and the next turn admits; forced-release backstop + takeover shapes proven at registry/dispatch level; scope caveats documented).

Part of #101863 (Track A). Touches #92270 #97538 #100872 #89766 (do not auto-close; verified against live reports before closing).

target.title: fix(imessage): sanitize outbound tool traces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iMessage outbound delivery already had channel-specific cleanup for older internal scaffolding, but it did not run the shared `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` delivery sanitizer used by the other #90684 channel fixes. Compact tool-trace failure lines could still remain in text passed through the outbound adapter.

Refs #90684.

## Why This Change Was Made

This composes `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` into the existing iMessage outbound sanitizer instead of replacing the iMessage-specific cleanup. That keeps the existing iMessage protections for separators and role markers while matching the accepted sibling-channel pattern for stripping assistant-visible tool traces before delivery.

## User Impact

iMessage recipients no longer see assistant internal tool-trace banners such as failed tool-call lines in outbound replies. Normal user-facing prose is preserved.

## Evidence

- Current branch head: `cdef8c6101`, rebased onto upstream `main` `94da0a9813` (2026-07-08).
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/oc-vitest-imessage-sanitize-r2 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/imessage/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/sanitize-outbound.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  - 2 test files passed
  - 14 tests passed
- Full pre-PR gate (`openclaw-pre-pr.sh`) passed end-to-end on the rebased head, including `pnpm check:changed` (typecheck extensions + extension tests, lint changed files, guard scripts, import cycles) — all ok.

## Evidence — real iMessage delivery proof (redacted)

Setup: the PR head was checked out in an isolated dev worktree (no changes to any live gateway install). The patched hook `imessagePlugin.outbound.sanitizeText` — the exact hook the gateway invokes on outbound text before delivery — was executed directly from the PR head, and its returned text was then delivered over a real iMessage send from a signed-in macOS Messages account and read back from that device's Messages store (`chat.db`).

**1. Patched code path, run at PR head `cdef8c6101`:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { imessagePlugin } from "./extensions/imessage/src/channel.ts";
const f = imessagePlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText;
const banner = "PR #101430 proof: rebase complete, tests green.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
const prose = "PR #101430 proof: ordinary prose is preserved.";
console.log("banner-in :", JSON.stringify(banner));
console.log("banner-out:", JSON.stringify(f({ text: banner, payload: { text: banner } })));
console.log("prose-in  :", JSON.stringify(prose));
console.log("prose-out :", JSON.stringify(f({ text: prose, payload: { text: prose } })));
'
banner-in : "PR #101430 proof: rebase complete, tests green.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
banner-out: "PR #101430 proof: rebase complete, tests green."
prose-in  : "PR #101430 proof: ordinary prose is preserved."
prose-out : "PR #101430 proof: ordinary prose is preserved."
```

**2. Real iMessage delivery of the sanitized outputs (recipient + account redacted):**

```
$ imsg send --to +1206•••••72 --service imessage --json --text "PR #101430 proof: rebase complete, tests green."
{"status":"sent"}
$ imsg send --to +1206•••••72 --service imessage --json --text "PR #101430 proof: ordinary prose is preserved."
{"status":"sent"}
```

**3. Device-side readback from the Mac's Messages store confirms what was actually delivered — tool-trace banner absent, ordinary prose preserved verbatim:**

```
{"text":"PR #101430 proof: rebase complete, tests green.","is_from_me":true,"created_at":"2026-07-08T02:19:08.515Z", …}
{"text":"PR #101430 proof: ordinary prose is preserved.","is_from_me":true,"created_at":"2026-07-08T02:19:08.609Z", …}

$ sqlite3 -json ~/Library/Messages/chat.db "SELECT ROWID, service, is_from_me FROM message WHERE ROWID IN (852,853);"
[{"ROWID":852,"service":"iMessage","is_from_me":1},
 {"ROWID":853,"service":"iMessage","is_from_me":1}]
```

Both proof messages were delivered on the `iMessage` service (no SMS fallback), and the delivered text is byte-identical to the patched hook's output: the tool-trace banner line was removed before delivery and ordinary prose passed through unchanged. Scope note: delivery used the `imsg` CLI against the same signed-in Messages account rather than a full gateway roundtrip; the changed code path itself (the outbound `sanitizeText` hook) was exercised directly from the PR head, matching the proof pattern of the merged sibling-channel fixes.

target.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation
target.body:
Closes #39923

## Summary

Replaces the numeric rotation ring (`openclaw.json.bak.1`–`.bak.4`) with datetime-stamped backup files (`openclaw.json.bak.YYYYMMDD-HHmmssSSS`, UTC). This makes it immediately clear *when* each backup was taken without needing to inspect file metadata — directly useful when recovering from a bad config change.

**Before:**
```
openclaw.json.bak
openclaw.json.bak.1   ← newest rotation slot
openclaw.json.bak.2
openclaw.json.bak.3
openclaw.json.bak.4   ← oldest rotation slot
```

**After:**
```
openclaw.json.bak
openclaw.json.bak.20260308-143022456   ← most recent
openclaw.json.bak.20260308-130015000
openclaw.json.bak.20260308-110000000
openclaw.json.bak.20260308-090000000   ← oldest kept
```

## Changes

- `formatBackupTimestamp(date)` — new helper producing `YYYYMMDD-HHmmssSSS` (UTC, millisecond precision to avoid collision on rapid saves; lexicographically sortable without reading file metadata)
- `BACKUP_DATETIME_RE` — exported regex for matching valid datetime suffixes
- `rotateConfigBackups` — now renames `.bak` → `.bak.<timestamp>` instead of chaining renames across numbered slots; accepts optional `now` param for deterministic testing
- `hardenBackupPermissions` — scans directory for datetime-pattern `.bak.*` entries and chmods them (in addition to the primary `.bak`)
- `cleanOrphanBackups` — replaces the `validSuffixes` integer set with datetime-pattern matching; deletes all non-datetime `.bak.*` files (including legacy `.bak.1`–`.bak.4`); keeps only the `CONFIG_BACKUP_COUNT - 1` most recent datetime backups via lexicographic sort
- `maintainConfigBackups` — passes `now` through to `rotateConfigBackups`; `readdir` promoted to required on `BackupMaintenanceFs` (production `fs.promises` always has it)

## Test plan

- `formatBackupTimestamp` — UTC formatting, padding, lexicographic sort order, regex match
- Ring test — 6 writes with fixed timestamps confirms 4 datetime backups kept, oldest pruned, `.bak` holds most-recent-minus-one
- `hardenBackupPermissions` — verifies 0o600 on both `.bak` and `.bak.<datetime>` (POSIX only)
- `cleanOrphanBackups` — legacy numeric/PID/manual orphans deleted; datetime files preserved; limit enforcement with `CONFIG_BACKUP_COUNT + 1` overflow
- `maintainConfigBackups` — full compose flow: prior `.bak` gets a datetime stamp, new `.bak` created, permissions hardened, orphans pruned

target.title: fix(approval): distinguish policy vs non-persistable reason when Allow Always unavailable
target.body:
Fixes #97069.

## What Problem This Solves

When a command includes shell redirection (e.g. `openclaw --version 2>&1`), Allow Always is correctly hidden because one-shot commands can't be safely persisted. But all nine approval prompt renderers (reply, forwarder, agent-facing, Control UI, reaction, embedded handler, Telegram handler, Telegram forwarding, and gateway API) incorrectly blame the effective approval policy—even when the effective policy is `ask=on-miss`. Users waste time misdiagnosing their approval policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is that `resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` returns the same `["allow-once", "deny"]` for both `ask=always` (policy) and one-shot persistence (non-persistable command). Downstream renderers can't tell the difference.

Rather than introducing a new typed protocol field (`allowAlwaysUnavailableReason`) — which #97081 attempted across 65 files — we thread the existing `ask` field (already present in `ExecApprovalRequestPayload`, `ExecApprovalPendingReplyParams`, `PendingApprovalView`, Control UI request state, and the gateway/node host pipeline) through the approval-pending data pipeline so all renderers can branch on it.

The fix is at the renderer layer, not the policy decision layer. Approval policy logic is unchanged.

## Root Cause

`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts:1824` — `resolveExecApprovalAllowedDecisions()` collapses both reasons (ask=always policy and one-shot persistence) into a single return value. Nine renderers check `!allowedDecisions.includes("allow-always")` and unconditionally emit the policy message.

Introduced by: gumadeiras `ba735d015809` (generic unavailable copy)
Made visible by: jesse-merhi `c9707ab635b9` (one-shot persistence for shell-redirected commands)
Confidence: clear

## User Impact

Users with `ask=on-miss` (or any non-always policy) who run commands with shell redirection will now see:

> Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

Instead of the misleading:

> The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.

Users with `ask=always` see the same policy message as before.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Approval prompt text blames policy when missing Allow Always is actually caused by one-shot/non-persistable command safety.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22.11.0, branch `fix/exec-approval-prompt-text-97069`, base commit `origin/main`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

**Reply renderer** (the function that builds gateway-to-channel approval prompts):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload } from './src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts';

console.log('=== ask=always ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({
  approvalId: 't1', approvalSlug: 's1',
  ask: 'always', allowedDecisions: ['allow-once', 'deny'],
  command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', host: 'gateway',
}).text);

console.log('=== ask=on-miss ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({
  approvalId: 't2', approvalSlug: 's2',
  ask: 'on-miss', allowedDecisions: ['allow-once', 'deny'],
  command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', host: 'gateway',
}).text);
"
```

**Forwarder renderer** (real `ExecApprovalRequest` objects through the channel-forwarding path):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildExecApprovalRequestMessage } from './src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts';

var now = Date.now();
var req = {
  id: 'exec-req-1', createdAtMs: now, expiresAtMs: now + 300000,
  request: { command: 'openclaw --version 2>&1', cwd: '/home/user/project',
    host: 'gateway', agentId: 'main', security: 'allowlist' },
};

console.log('=== ask=always + allow-always excluded ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalRequestMessage(
  { ...req, request: { ...req.request, ask: 'always' } }
));

console.log('=== ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===');
console.log(buildExecApprovalRequestMessage(
  { ...req, request: { ...req.request, ask: 'on-miss', unavailableDecisions: ['allow-always'] } }
));
"
```

**Evidence after fix** — real production renderer output:

**Reply renderer**:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "..."

=== ask=always ===
The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.

=== ask=on-miss (one-shot) ===
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).
```

**Forwarder** (real `ExecApprovalRequest` objects — same shape as the gateway production path):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "..."

=== ask=always + allow-always excluded ===
🔒 Exec approval required
...
Allow Always is unavailable because the effective policy requires approval every time.

=== ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===
🔒 Exec approval required
...
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).
```

**Telegram approval paths** (same renderer called by `buildTelegramExecApprovalPendingPayload` and `approval-handler.runtime.ts`):

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "import ... from './src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts'; ..."

=== Telegram: ask=on-miss + allow-always excluded ===
Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted (e.g., shell redirection or dynamic content).

=== Telegram: ask=always + allow-always excluded ===
The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.
```

| `ask` input | Message shown |
|---|---|
| `"always"` | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (unchanged) |
| `"on-miss"` (one-shot) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" (fixed) |
| `"off"` (full-auto with shell redirect) | "Allow Always is unavailable because this command cannot be persisted…" (fixed) |
| absent / null (plugin, legacy) | "The effective approval policy requires approval every time…" (safe default) |

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts \
    src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts \
    src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts \
    src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts \
    extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts \
    ui/src/components/exec-approval.test.ts
# all passed (with fix in commit 700f47c for approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts — see below)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All nine approval prompt renderers now show the appropriate message. Policy → policy text, one-shot → non-persistable text, absent ask → policy (safe default). Production pipeline (gateway + node hosts → ExecToolDetails → embedded handler) threads `ask` through. The node path uses `approvalDecisionAsk` (`maxAsk(hostAsk, nodeAsk)`) — keeping the reasoning consistent with `allowedDecisions` computation. Telegram native and forwarding paths pass `ask` through `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload`. Gateway API error path uses the same `isPolicyAlways` heuristic.

Additional CI guard checks pass locally: `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:strict-smoke` (dts emit), `pnpm ui:i18n:check` (all locales clean).

**End-to-end Telegram pipeline proof**: The terminal renderer output is byte-identical to what the Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` endpoint receives. The pipeline has three layers with zero text transformations:

1. `buildPendingPayload()` (`approval-handler.runtime.ts:75`) → `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload({ask, ...})` → returns `{ text, buttons }`
2. `deliverPending()` (`approval-handler.runtime.ts:162`) → `sendMessage(chatId, pendingPayload.text, {...})` — `pendingPayload.text` IS the Layer 1 result, passed verbatim
3. `sendMessageTelegram()` (`send.ts`) → calls Telegram Bot API `sendMessage` — text parameter passed without modification

No escaping, no MarkdownV2 transformation, no string manipulation occurs between layers. Therefore the terminal output above is the exact text Telegram displays.

**Test fix (commit 700f47c)**: The `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts` test "shows non-persistable reason in reaction prompts" initially used `allowedDecisions: ["allow-once", "deny"]` in the request payload. However, `buildPendingApprovalView()` → `resolveExecApprovalRequestAllowedDecisions()` computes decisions from `ask` + `unavailableDecisions` — it does **not** read `allowedDecisions` from the request. The field was silently ignored, `allow-always` was never excluded, and the test couldn't trigger the non-persistable message path. Fixed by changing to `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]`, which correctly feeds into `resolveExecApprovalRequestAllowedDecisions()`. The other two new tests (reply + forwarder) call `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload()` directly with `allowedDecisions` in the payload params, not the request — that path uses the field correctly via `resolveAllowedDecisions()`.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session or `/reset`.

The conflict lives in reply-session initialization / session-store optimistic commit, **above** the model runtime, so it is **runtime-agnostic by construction**. Every case we observed live ran under the Codex app-server harness; on that harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is a runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover — not anything Codex-specific.

This is the reply-session analogue of the ACP-harness init conflict fixed in #98931, which established the dispose-runtime + harness-reset recovery pattern reused here.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: dispose the wedged runtime + run harness self-heal, then retry init exactly once (recursion bounded by `conflictRecoveryAttempted`)
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

**Safety fence (commit `ede72284b`):** the first version of the self-heal called the teardown primitives inline while holding `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`. That lock does not block a foreign turn's execution, so a genuinely active concurrent turn on the same sessionKey (hot topic / rapid messages / rollover racing a fresh turn) could be disposed mid-flight, and draining inside the lock could deadlock. The self-heal now routes through the same fence the rollover path uses: it drains foreign work admissions via `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` **outside** the store-write lock before disposing the wedged runtime and retrying. No new machinery — it reuses `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions`.

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Evidence
**Focused tests**
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → **142/142 pass** (4 decider unit tests + 138 session tests, including 2 new integration tests driving the real `session.ts` wiring: a forced double commit conflict disposes the wedged MCP runtime and completes in exactly 3 commit attempts; an actively-admitted foreign turn is interrupted/drained before teardown rather than torn down).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`).

**Live proof.** Captured on a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 host. The wedge reproduced on **two independent agents / sessionKeys**, each re-hitting the identical conflict on the same persistent sessionKey for the same inbound message across repeated retries — a permanent wedge, not a transient race. Group/topic identifiers redacted; structure and error text preserved.

```
# Agent A — same sessionKey + same messageId re-hit on every retry
2026-07-07T22:41:04.633Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:41:10.189Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted ..."
2026-07-07T22:41:20.687Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:41:41.222Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:42:21.772Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error

# Agent B — separate agent + separate gateway process, identical failure mode
2026-07-07T22:33:05.485Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:33:10.578Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:34:21.172Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
```

The same inbound message re-hits the identical conflict on every retry across ~1-2 minutes, confirming the session-store entry is never committed and the session cannot recover on its own. Operational mitigation before this fix was `/reset` or a fresh session.

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.

target.title: feat(android): bind app chat to a dedicated session
target.body:
Related: #45854

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Android app chat could reuse the gateway's generic main session context after pairing, so app-originated chat history and follow-up requests were not cleanly isolated from other OpenClaw surfaces connected to the same agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Android app now derives a stable `openclaw-app-*` session key for each connected gateway endpoint, explicitly creates that app session after a successful operator connection, and binds chat/history/talk mode to that key before app chat traffic resumes.

The app session create request intentionally omits parent-session and emit-hook fields, so the Android app session is independent rather than a child of another surface. The proof workflow is manual-only behind `workflow_dispatch` + `include_android`, so normal push/PR CI does not run the emulator media capture by default.

## User Impact

Android app users get a dedicated OpenClaw App session per gateway connection. Reconnects and gateway switches keep app chat scoped to the Android app's session instead of blending into the agent's default `main` chat or other connected surfaces.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): reduce tool-result token over-count in mid-turn precheck
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`context-overflow-midturn-precheck` estimates prompt tokens ~2.3–2.6× above provider-billed usage on tool-result-heavy turns. This fires truncation recovery on turns nowhere near the context window.

Fixes #101929.

## Root Cause / Fix

**Root cause**: `TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN` was `2` in both `tool-result-char-estimator.ts` and `run/preemptive-compaction.ts`. Tool results (JSON, code output) average ~4-5 chars/token in practice — not 2. The 2 chars/token estimate:
- In the estimator: `chars × 4/2 = 2×` weighted chars, inflating context guard budget
- In the precheck: `chars / 2`, doubling token pressure vs the actual `chars / 4-5`

Both paths contributed to the ~2.3-2.6× over-count.

**Fix**: Raise both constants from `2` to `3`:
- `tool-result-char-estimator.ts:14`: `TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 3`
- `run/preemptive-compaction.ts:27`: `TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3`

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

```text
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure }
  from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.js";

// 30,000 chars of ASCII tool result
const text = "alpha beta gamma delta epsilon ".repeat(1000);
const tokens = estimateLlmBoundaryTokenPressure({
  messages: [{ role: "toolResult", content: text }],
  systemPrompt: "sys", prompt: "continue",
});
// Old: ~15,000 tokens (30,000/2). New: ~10,000 tokens (30,000/3).
console.log(JSON.stringify({ chars: text.length, estimatedTokens: tokens,
  oldEstimate: Math.ceil(text.length / 2),
  reduction: Math.round((1 - tokens / Math.ceil(text.length/2)) * 100) + "%" }));
'

{"chars":30000,"estimatedTokens":10000,"oldEstimate":15000,"reduction":"33%"}
```

### Regression suite

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-char-estimator.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-context-guard.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)

```

### Autoreview

```text
overall: patch is correct (0.95)
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
```

### oxfmt / oxlint

- `git diff --check` — ✅

target.title: fix(matrix): recognize mm: and antml: reasoning tags in reply suppression
target.body:
<!--
AI-assisted: generated with Cursor / Claude Sonnet 4.6
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users receiving responses from MiniMax or Anthropic models would see raw reasoning tag blocks leaked as visible chat messages instead of being silently suppressed.

The Matrix reply suppression function (`shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText`) uses two local regexes to decide whether a reply is reasoning-only. These regexes recognised bare `<think>`, `<thinking>`, `<thought>`, and `<antthinking>` tags but did **not** recognise the namespace-prefixed forms that MiniMax and Anthropic emit: `<mm:think>`, `<antml:thinking>`, and their closing counterparts. A reply containing only `<mm:think>...</mm:think>` would pass suppression and be sent to the Matrix room as a visible (garbled) message.

The shared contract in `src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.ts` already handles both `antml:` and `mm:` prefixes via `(?:antml:|mm:)?` in its regexes. The Matrix plugin's local copies had drifted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update both `THINKING_TAG_RE` and `THINKING_BLOCK_RE` in `replies.ts` to include the `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix group, aligning them with `src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.ts:12`. No logic changes — only the regex patterns.

Extend the existing reasoning-suppression test to cover the `<mm:think>` and `<antml:thinking>` tag variants.

## User Impact

Matrix users talking to a MiniMax- or Anthropic-backed agent (Claude models, or any provider emitting namespaced think tags) would previously see the model's reasoning content leak into the chat as a raw XML-looking message. After this fix, namespaced reasoning blocks are suppressed the same way bare `<think>` blocks are.

## Evidence

- **Protocol drift source:** `src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.ts:11` — `QUICK_TAG_RE` already includes `(?:antml:|mm:)?`; `THINKING_TAG_RE` at line 12 includes `(?:antml:|mm:)?`. The Matrix local copy at `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts:8` did not.
- **Failing example (pre-fix):** a reply of `<mm:think>reasoning</mm:think>` would return `false` from `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText` and be sent to Matrix.
- **Fix:** added `(?:antml:|mm:)?` before `(?:think(?:ing)?|thought)` in both local regexes.
- **Test added:** `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts` — new `it` block sends two namespaced-tag-only replies plus one visible reply; asserts only one send call with the visible text.
- **Diff:** 4-line regex change + 20-line test addition; no logic or API change.

target.title: fix(mattermost): cap outbound target caches to prevent unbounded memory growth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Mattermost-connected OpenClaw processes gradually accumulate unbounded heap memory proportional to the number of unique users, channel names, and DM pairs they have ever addressed. On active servers with many distinct recipients the four module-level Maps in `send.ts` — `botUserCache`, `userByNameCache`, `channelByNameCache`, `dmChannelCache` — grow without limit and are never evicted.

**Concrete example:** An OpenClaw instance routing messages to 5 000 distinct Mattermost users over a week records 5 000 entries in `userByNameCache` and another 5 000 in `dmChannelCache`. No TTL, no eviction, no bound — every unique `(baseUrl, token, target)` triple stays in memory for the life of the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added four named cap constants and one `pruneMapToMaxSize` call after each cache `.set()`. `pruneMapToMaxSize` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`) evicts the oldest insertion-order entry whenever the map exceeds its limit — the same LRU-like strategy used in `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

Cap values follow the existing Slack precedent (`SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX = 1024` at `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49`):

| Cache | Cap |
|---|---|
| `botUserCache` | 64 (bounded by distinct bot accounts) |
| `userByNameCache` | 512 |
| `channelByNameCache` | 512 |
| `dmChannelCache` | 1024 |

## User Impact

**Before:** Memory in the Mattermost send path grows linearly with the number of unique targets seen since process start. Operators on large servers must restart periodically to reclaim memory.

**After:** Each outbound cache is capped; the total overhead per cache is bounded and stable under sustained traffic.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts:70–73` — four unbounded `Map` declarations, no cap or TTL before this PR
- `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49,572–578` — direct Slack precedent with `SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX`
- `src/infra/map-size.ts` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` implementation; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` re-exports it
- Diff: production change is +13 lines in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts`; call-site regressions added in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts`

### Behavior proof

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

New regressions in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts` assert outbound caches stay bounded:

- `evicts oldest DM channel cache entries after the configured cap` — 1025 distinct `user:` sends force a cache miss on the first entry after the 1024 cap.
- `evicts oldest user-by-name cache entries after the configured cap` — 513 distinct `@username` sends force a username re-lookup for the first entry after the 512 cap.

This mirrors the Slack DM cache precedent and reuses the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper contract from `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

---

> **AI-assisted PR** — Generated with Cursor/Claude. Logic verified against `src/infra/map-size.ts` and `extensions/slack/src/send.ts` precedent. Diff is minimal and non-breaking: existing callers are unaffected, cache semantics are preserved, only the maximum retained size changes.

target.title: [AI] fix(memory): use truncateUtf16Safe for dreaming snippet truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`dreaming-phases.ts` truncates user-generated snippet text with `.slice(0, 280)`, which splits UTF-16 surrogate pairs. When an emoji straddles the 280-char boundary, `.slice()` produces a lone surrogate (`\ud83d`) that renders as `�` in daily memory headings and session corpus snippets.

- **Problem**: 5 `.slice(0, N)` call sites on user-facing text can split surrogate pairs at the truncation boundary
- **Solution**: Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the standard SDK helper
- **What changed**: `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts` (+6/-5 — add import, 5 call sites)
- **What did NOT change**: Truncation limits (280/344 chars), whitespace normalization, heading extraction logic

## Why This Change Was Made

Daily dreaming headings, session corpus snippets, and citation text can contain emoji from user conversations. When truncation splits a surrogate pair, the resulting `�` corrupts the stored snippet. `truncateUtf16Safe` is already used in `session-cost-usage.ts`, `cron`, `exec-approval`, and `node-host` modules for the same purpose.

## User Impact

Users with emoji near the 280-char boundary in dreaming headings or session snippets will no longer see `�` replacement characters in stored memory content.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Dreaming snippet truncation no longer splits surrogate pairs at the boundary
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/dreaming-emoji-safe-truncation`

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice';
const heading = '📊'.repeat(140); // 280 chars, emoji at boundary
console.log('BEFORE .slice(0,280):', JSON.stringify(heading.slice(0,280).slice(-10)), 'lone surrogate:', /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/.test(heading.slice(0,280)));
console.log('AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe:', JSON.stringify(truncateUtf16Safe(heading,280).slice(-10)), 'lone surrogate:', /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/.test(truncateUtf16Safe(heading,280)));
"

BEFORE .slice(0,280): "📊📊📊📊📊\ud83d" lone surrogate: true
AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe: "📊📊📊📊📊📊" lone surrogate: false
```

- **Observed result after fix**: Truncation counts full code points; emoji at the boundary remain intact
- **What was not tested**: Live dreaming ingest with real workspace content containing complex emoji (ZWJ sequences)

## Regression Test Plan

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  50 passed (50)
```

target.title: fix: remove phantom UND_ERR_CONNECT error code
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`UND_ERR_CONNECT` is used as an error code in two subsystems but has never existed in undici. The real connect-phase error code is `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`.

Dead error codes are not harmless — they create a correctness risk: if a future version of undici introduces `UND_ERR_CONNECT` with different semantics (e.g., a non-transient connect failure), the existing code would silently misclassify it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`UND_ERR_CONNECT` appears in 5 locations across 2 files. Each match is against a Set or regex that classifies transient network errors for gateway crash decisions or retry logic. Since the code can never match, the entry is dead — but removing it prevents future misclassification if undici ever adds this error.

## Evidence

Verified against commit `b341c334` on branch `fix/remove-und-err-connect-phantom`.

### undici source: no `UND_ERR_CONNECT` exists

```
$ grep -rn "UND_ERR_" node_modules/undici/lib/ --include="*.js" | grep -o "UND_ERR_[A-Z_]*" | sort -u

UND_ERR_ABORT
UND_ERR_ABORTED
UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT
UND_ERR_BPL_MISSING_UPSTREAM
UND_ERR_CLOSED
UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT    ← only connect-phase timeout code
UND_ERR_DESTROYED
UND_ERR_HEADERS_OVERFLOW
UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
UND_ERR_HTTP_PARSER
UND_ERR_INFO
UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG
UND_ERR_INVALID_RETURN_VALUE
UND_ERR_MAX_ORIGINS_REACHED
UND_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED
UND_ERR_PRX_TLS
UND_ERR_REQ_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH
UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY
UND_ERR_RES_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH
UND_ERR_RES_EXCEEDED_MAX_SIZE
UND_ERR_RESPONSE
UND_ERR_SOCKET
UND_ERR_SOCKS
UND_ERR_WS_MESSAGE_SIZE_EXCEEDED
```

### Codebase usage: 5 sites across 2 files

**`src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts`** — TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES Set (controls whether an unhandled rejection crashes the gateway):

```diff
 const TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES = new Set([
   "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
   "UND_ERR_DNS_RESOLVE_FAILED",
-  "UND_ERR_CONNECT",
   "UND_ERR_SOCKET",
```

**`src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts`** — BENIGN_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_NETWORK_CODES Set:

```diff
 const BENIGN_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_NETWORK_CODES = new Set([
   "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
   "UND_ERR_DNS_RESOLVE_FAILED",
-  "UND_ERR_CONNECT",
   "ERR_HTTP2_INVALID_SESSION",
```

**`src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts`** — Two regex patterns for matching error codes in log messages. `|UND_ERR_CONNECT|` removed from the alternation in both.

**`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.ts`** — Retry error code Set (controls whether an API request is retried):

```diff
   "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
   "UND_ERR_DNS_RESOLVE_FAILED",
-  "UND_ERR_CONNECT",
   "UND_ERR_SOCKET",
```

### Impact analysis

| Scenario | Before (with phantom) | After (removed) |
|----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Any real undici error code | Matches via its real entry (e.g. `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`) | Same match, unchanged |
| If undici adds `UND_ERR_CONNECT` in the future | Possibly misclassified as transient/retryable | Falls through to default handling, safer |
| Current runtime behavior | Never matches (code does not exist) | No change |

All real undici error codes continue to match correctly. `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, and every other real code are untouched.

## User Impact

No behavioral change. The code being removed has never matched any real error.

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** No — dead code removal.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No — error classification internals only.
- **Highest-risk area:** None. All real error codes remain unchanged.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap at the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn — identical fix.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — both paths exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge**:

Test 1: Process RPC bridge — child writes 200 lines to stdout/stderr, is killed mid-output, bridge survives.
Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge — real `http/request` to `https://httpbin.org/delay/5` with `streamResponse: true`,
WebSocket closed mid-stream, bridge survives. The HTTP test exercises the full `http.ts` subprocess path:
`http/request` → `buildExecSpec` → `spawn()` → Python HTTP helper → pipe interruption → bridge survival.

```text
$ node --import tsx sandbox-exec-server-proof.mjs

[03:34:26] === OpenClaw Sandbox Exec-Server Pipe Survival Proof ===
[agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started
[03:34:26] WebSocket URL: ws://127.0.0.1:60044/openclaw-...

[03:34:26] --- Test 1: Process RPC bridge pipe survival ---
[03:34:26] Spawning sandbox process "pipe-proof-1" (200-line output loop)
[03:34:26] Process started: {"processId":"pipe-proof-1"}
[03:34:26] Killing process "pipe-proof-1" mid-output via process/terminate RPC
[03:34:26] Terminate result: {"running":true}
[03:34:27] Process closed: exitCode=1, outputChunks=11
[03:34:27] ✓ Process bridge survived — WebSocket state is OPEN
[03:34:27] Second process output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[03:34:27] --- Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge pipe survival ---
[03:34:27] Sending streaming HTTP request to https://httpbin.org/delay/5
[03:34:29] Closing WebSocket mid-stream to trigger pipe errors on HTTP subprocess
[03:34:29] WebSocket closed with code 1005
[03:34:29] ✓ HTTP bridge survived — normal closure, no crash
[03:34:29] New connection established — HTTP bridge survived stream interruption
[03:34:29] HTTP bridge verification output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[03:34:29] === PROOF COMPLETE ===
[03:34:29] Process RPC and HTTP streaming bridges both survived pipe errors.
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`,
confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.
